## ising-model

Lean 4 + mathlib formalization of Ising model theorems, with particular
emphasis on Glimm–Jaffe, *Quantum Physics: A Functional Integral Point of
View* (2nd ed., 1987).

> **Notice:** automatic publication of the doc-gen4 API reference to

All theorems are formally proved with **zero `sorry`** and **zero declared
axioms** — the formalization is now fully axiom-free (modulo Mathlib).
`polynomialDecay_contraction_factor_tendsto` (the last declared axiom) was
discharged as a **theorem** (`TheoremEtaLe1/Contraction.lean`): the boundary edge
count is `O(r^{d-1})` (a *surface* bound, `latticeBallBoundaryEdges_card_le_sphere`
+ `latticeSphere_card_le'`), each endpoint sits at distance `∈ {r, r+1}` where
polynomial decay forces `corr∞·dist^{d-1} ≤ δ`, and the volume-cancelling product
`O(r^{d-1})·O(r^{-(d-1)})·δ` is made small. With this, **GJ §17.8 Theorem 17.8.1
(`η ≤ 1`) is unconditional**.
`shellSup_contraction` was discharged as a **theorem**
(`TheoremEtaLe1/Contraction.lean`) as the shell supremum of
`ball_boundary_tight_infinite` (with the corrected `1 ≤ r` hypothesis threaded
through the contraction / high-temperature / cubic-shell consumers);
`ball_boundary_tight_infinite` was discharged as a
**theorem** (`TheoremEtaLe1/BallBoundaryInfinite.lean`) — the formalization
revealed the original axiom was false for `r = 0` and for
`latticeDistance d 0 x = r + 1`, so the proved theorem carries the corrected
hypotheses `1 ≤ r` and `r + 1 < latticeDistance d 0 x` (the distance condition is
supplied by the downstream `shellSup_contraction`, whose shell points have
distance `≥ r + 2`; `1 ≤ r` must additionally be threaded into it);
the GHS-corollary Lebowitz axioms were fully discharged in PRs
#3909–#3911 (two of them were false as stated and were replaced by
corrected proven theorems), `cor_4_3_3_scaled` was proven in PR #3912
via the abstract-weight duplicate-variable layer, and
`phi4_single_site_nonneg` was proven unconditionally in PR #3917 by the
four-fold sign symmetrisation; see the *Axioms* section below.

## How to read this page

We distinguish three formalization regimes:

1. **Finite-volume** — the Ising model on a fixed finite graph
   `G : SimpleGraph ι` with `[Fintype ι]`.  Most of the project is here.
2. **Discretized infinite-volume** — a fixed finite ambient `ι` with
   growing subgraphs `G₁ ≤ G₂ ≤ ⋯`.  The "Λ ↑" convergence theorems
   of GJ §4.2 and §4.6 are formalized here: the mechanism of proof is
   identical to GJ, but the ambient lattice is finite.
3. **Genuine infinite-volume** — an unbounded ambient type `V : Type*`
   with `Λ : Finset V` finite volumes and an exhaustion `Λₙ ↑ V`.
   Introduced in `IsingModel/AmbientLattice.lean`.

When a GJ theorem is marked "Done", the adjacent *Regime* column
specifies which of the three above apply.

### §4.2: Thermodynamic limit of correlations (Thm 4.2.3)

Original GJ statement: as `Λ ↑ ℝᵈ`, `⟨σ^B⟩_Λ` converges.
Formalized in three regimes:

| Result | Statement | File | Regime |
|---|---|---|---|
| `correlation_convergent` | `⟨σ^A⟩_{(n,h,β)}` converges as `J = n → ∞` | `InfiniteVolume.lean` | Finite |
| `correlation_convergent_h` | `⟨σ^A⟩_{(J,n,β)}` converges as `h = n → ∞` | `InfiniteVolume.lean` | Finite |
| `correlation_convergent_beta` | `⟨σ^A⟩_{(J,h,n+1)}` converges as `β = n+1 → ∞` | `InfiniteVolume.lean` | Finite |
| `correlation_convergent_subgraph` | `⟨σ^A⟩_{Gₙ}` converges for `Gₙ ↑` | `InfiniteVolume.lean` | Discretized Λ↑ |
| `Ambient.correlationInfinite` | `correlationInfinite := ⨆ n, correlationAlongExhaustion G Λ p A n` | `AmbientLattice.lean` | **Genuine ∞-vol (full)**: convergence, Λ-independence, GKS-I/II, J/h/β monotonicity |

Named specializations at `A = {i}`:
- Finite / Discretized: `magnetization_convergent_{J,h,beta,subgraph}`
- Genuine ∞-vol: `Ambient.magnetizationInfinite`
  (nonneg / le_one / indep_exhaustion / monotone_{J,h,beta} inherited from `correlationInfinite`)

| `Ambient.freeEnergyAlongExhaustion_latticeGraph_cubicExhaustion_tendsto` (**Prop 4.6.1, unconditional on ℤ^d**) | `Tendsto (freeEnergyAlongExhaustion (latticeGraph d) (cubicExhaustion d) p) atTop (𝓝 freeEnergyInfinite)` for ferromagnetic `p` — no superadditivity or tower hypotheses. **Status (as of PR #2729).** The
local-branch form of GJ Thm 4.6.2 finite-volume analyticity is
formalised: `exists_freeEnergyComplex_analyticAt_branch_of_leeYangDomain`
gives, at every `h₀ ∈ leeYangDomain`, an analytic function `f` with
`exp(|ι|·f(h₀)) = Z(h₀)` and `f(h₀) = freeEnergyComplex(h₀)`
(basepoint). Additionally, the Vitali bridge
`vitali_bridge_leeYangDomain` and all modulus bounds
(`norm_partitionFunctionComplex_le_*`,
`norm_freeEnergyComplex_le_trivial_bound`) are in place. The conditional
along-exhaustion Vitali assembly
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_vitali_bridge_leeYangDomain_identified_at_real`
now packages the final handoff from locally uniform convergence to
Lee-Yang holomorphicity and real-axis identification with
`freeEnergyInfinite`. The along-exhaustion per-stage branch wrappers
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_analyticBranch_leeYangDomain_all_stages`
and
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_analyticOnNhd_branch_ball_all_stages`
also package the finite-stage Lee-Yang local branches needed before a
future normal-family argument. The strong ball-level wrappers
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_analyticOnNhd_branch_ball_all_stages_strong`
add basepoint normalisation to the same local witness. The local branch-family
assembly
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_vitali_ball_identified_at_center`
now consumes a locally-uniformly convergent chosen branch family on a ball and
identifies the centre value with `↑freeEnergyInfinite`. The local-cover
handoff
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_vitali_localCover_real`
globalises this conditional statement: if every Lee-Yang point has a local
branch-family witness converging to the same `f`, then `f` is holomorphic on
`leeYangDomain`; under `BoundedEdgeDensity G Λ`,
`DisjointTowerHypotheses G Λ p`, and `(p.h : ℂ) ∈ leeYangDomain`, it also
agrees with `freeEnergyInfinite` at the real centre. PR #2693 adds the
corresponding subsequence-indexed handoff
`Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_subseq_branchFamily_vitali_localCover_real`:
after a Montel-style extraction with a strictly increasing stage map `σ`, the
same local-cover Vitali and real-axis identification conclusions apply to
branch families whose identities are written at stage `σ m`. The compact-uniform
`Z_ℂ` input
`Ambient.norm_partitionFunctionComplexAlongExhaustion_le_on_isCompact_stage`
now supplies a single real-part bound for all `h` in a compact field set and
all stages of the exhaustion, with the numerical right-hand side still allowed
to depend on the stage. Under bounded edge density and nonvanishing, the upper
normalised-log bridge
`Ambient.exists_real_log_norm_partitionFunctionComplexAlongExhaustion_div_card_le_on_isCompact`
turns it into a stage-independent upper bound for
`Real.log ‖Z_{Λ_n}(h)‖ / |Λ_n|` on compact field sets. On compact subsets of
`leeYangDomain`, `Ambient.exists_log_norm_partitionFunctionComplexAlongExhaustion_div_card_le_leeYangDomain`
uses Lee-Yang nonvanishing to discharge that nonzero hypothesis under
`β > 0`, `J > 0`. This still provides only the upper side of the absolute-log
estimate. The normalised-log bridge
`Ambient.norm_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_le_of_abs_log_norm_bound_on_set`
then records the conditional passage from a uniform
`|log ‖Z_{Λ_n}(h)‖| / |Λ_n|` bound to the corresponding principal
free-energy bound; deriving that normalised-log bound remains part of the
future normal-family construction. The stage-independent form
`Ambient.norm_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_le_of_abs_log_norm_bound_on_set_uniform`
packages the resulting locally bounded family as `‖f_n(h)‖ ≤ C + π` on the
same set. PRs #2683-#2691 packaged the Lee-Yang upper/lower-log handoff, the
compact fugacity gap, finite-stage polynomial and `Z_ℂ` lower bounds, the
conditional polynomial-witness lower-log bridge, and compact/ball/point-local
conditional locally bounded wrappers. PR #2692 discharges that remaining
polynomial-witness lower normalised-log input on compact subsets of
`leeYangDomain`: it introduces the one-variable specialization
`MultilinPoly.uniformPolynomial`, proves the root-product estimate
`Polynomial.one_sub_radius_pow_natDegree_le_norm_eval_of_roots_norm_ge_one`,
and applies Lee-Yang nonvanishing to show that the specialized Ising
polynomial has constant value `q(0)=1` and all roots outside the open unit
disk. If the compact fugacity gap gives `‖exp(-2βh)‖ ≤ r < 1` on
`K ⊆ leeYangDomain`, the resulting witness is
`ε_n=(1-r)^|Λ_n|`, with `Real.log ε_n / |Λ_n| = Real.log (1-r)`. Thus
`Ambient.exists_poly_lower_norm_isingEdgePoly_eval_leeYangFugacityVec_on_isCompact`
and
`Ambient.exists_lower_log_norm_partitionFunctionComplexAlongExhaustion_leeYang_of_isCompact`
provide the stage-uniform lower normalised-log bound without an external
polynomial-witness hypothesis. The unconditional locally bounded family
wrappers
`Ambient.exists_norm_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_le_leeYang_of_isCompact`,
`Ambient.exists_norm_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_le_leeYang_on_ball`, and
`Ambient.exists_norm_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_le_leeYang_around`, plus
their ℤ^d wrappers in `PerStageComplex.lean`, now supply the local boundedness
input needed for the remaining normal-family/Vitali branch construction. PRs
#2694-#2696 package the compact-open extraction handoff on one ball, then on
two balls, then on a finite family of Lee-Yang balls, producing one common
strictly increasing subsequence and local differentiable limits under explicit
compact-open compactness hypotheses. PR #2697 adds the explicit-overlap
handoff: if the selected stage branches are eventually equal on every pairwise
overlap, then the extracted local limits agree pairwise on those overlaps. PR
#2698 adds the finite local-patching handoff, patching such compatible local
limits to one differentiable function on the finite union of balls. PR #2699
adds the open-cover patching handoff, replacing the finite-index restriction
with an arbitrary compatible open cover whose union covers `leeYangDomain`.
PR #2700 packages that open-cover handoff for the canonical pointed cover by
Lee-Yang balls indexed by the points of `leeYangDomain`. PR #2701 packages
each point-centred ball's branch-limit witness into
`Ambient.LeeYangLocalBranchLimit` and patches compatible point-indexed
structured data through the same pointed local-cover assembly. PR #2702 adds
the corresponding structured-data real-centre identification wrapper. PR
#2703 packages the data and compatibility into one
`Ambient.LeeYangLocalBranchLimitFamily` endpoint. PR #2704 adds the
real-centred package `Ambient.LeeYangRealBranchLimitFamily`, including
Lee-Yang membership of the real centre and centre normalisation. PR #2705
packages finite compact-open diagonal/overlap output as
`Ambient.LeeYangFiniteSubseqBranchLimitFamily`, with a patching wrapper for the
finite union of balls. PR #2706 adds the corresponding finite packaged
real-centre identification wrapper. PR #2707 composes the compact-open finite
package extraction directly with that real-centre patch. PR #2708 adds the
corresponding compact-open extraction-to-patch wrapper without the real-centre
identification conclusion. PR #2728 connects the pre-Montel
`LeeYangPointwiseNormalisedAllStageBranchData` package to that finite
compact-open extraction and finite patch endpoint for selected Lee-Yang
centres, still under explicit compact-open compactness and overlap-equality
hypotheses. PR #2709 packages finite Lee-Yang cover geometry,
and PR #2729 gives the direct all-stage-data finite Lee-Yang cover bridge using
the radii and Lee-Yang-domain containment already stored in the all-stage
package. PR #2730 adds the all-stage selected real-centre and compact-target
finite-cover patch wrappers, identifying the real-centre value with
`↑freeEnergyInfinite` on compact targets covered by the selected balls.
PR #2731 extracts the selected finite all-stage balls from compactness of
`K`, packages the real-centred `Fin n` geometry, and feeds that geometry back
into the PR #2730 compact real-cover patch bridge.
PR #2710 bundles the selected real-centre index, and PR #2711 adds the compact
target `K` covered by those finite balls.

**Not yet formalized** (future PRs):
- Montel-style locally uniform convergence/subsequence extraction of local
  Lee-Yang branch families from the now-unconditional local boundedness plus
  real-axis Fekete and the branch-family identity theorem; PRs #2694-#2711
  provide post-extraction and conditional patching handoffs through finite
  Lee-Yang covers, finite real-centred cover packages, compact finite targets, arbitrary open covers,
  the pointed Lee-Yang ball cover, and structured local-cover branch-limit
  data, but mathlib still lacks a direct Montel theorem.
- Coherent branch-family construction giving the explicit overlap hypothesis,
  and diagonal coherent local-cover extraction supplying the compatible
  open-cover input.
- Note: the principal-branch `freeEnergyComplex` may be discontinuous
  where `Z` crosses the negative real axis; the local-branch form
  is the mathematically correct statement of GJ Thm 4.6.2.

The contour sum is restricted to **connected** spin droplets, the foundation of the volume-independent contour counting for the low-temperature `m*(β)>0`. `ReachableWithin G T x y` — reachability via a `G`-walk staying inside `T`. `downComponent G σ i` — the connected component of `i` in the down-spins (vertices `ReachableWithin (downSpins σ)` from `i`); `self_mem_downComponent`, `downComponent_subset_downSpins` (for `σ_i=-1`). `cutEdges_downComponent_subset_phaseBoundary` — **the key contour fact**: when `σ_i=-1`, every cut edge of the droplet lies in the phase boundary `∂σ` (a cut edge joins a droplet down-spin to a non-droplet up-spin). `IsConnectedDroplet`, `isConnectedDroplet_downComponent` (the droplet is connected, through `i`, via `ReachableWithin` symmetry). `indicator_spin_down_le_connected_contour_sum` — `1_{σ_i=↓} ≤ ∑_{S∋i, connected} 1_{cut S ⊆ ∂σ}` (the connected refinement of `indicator_spin_down_le_contour_sum`, witnessed by `downComponent`). Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `ConnectedDroplet.lean` | Finite, connected refinement |

| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The ray-exit anchored route** — `Peierls/RayExitAnchoredRoute.lean`. `dartReachable_of_rayExitAnchored` specializes the abstract anchored reachability route to the concrete map `rayExitAnchorDartMap F`; `dartDualCut_isEdgeConnected_of_rayExitAnchored`, `dualCutSub_isEdgeConnected_of_rayExitAnchored`, and `dualCutInBox_isEdgeConnected_of_rayExitAnchored` carry the same specialization through the ambient, subtype, and common-box dual cuts. `peierls_contour_count_rayExit_anchored` specializes the count consumer so each droplet uses `rayExitAnchorDartMap` as its anchor map. The remaining inputs are still explicit: every boundary dart must reach the ray-exit anchor of its left site, adjacent sites of `F` must have reachable ray-exit anchors, and ordinary within-`F` connectivity chains those local steps. Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `RayExitAnchoredRoute.lean` | Ray-exit anchored route |
| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The ray-exit shadow route** — `Peierls/RayExitShadowRoute.lean`. `dartReachable_of_rayExitShadow` replaces the per-edge `DartReachable` step of the ray-exit anchored route with a shared-dual-vertex shadow: adjacent sites of `F` must have ray-exit anchor edges sharing some vertex, and `dartReachable_of_shared` turns that shadow into the step. `dartDualCut_isEdgeConnected_of_rayExitShadow`, `dualCutSub_isEdgeConnected_of_rayExitShadow`, and `dualCutInBox_isEdgeConnected_of_rayExitShadow` carry the shadow input through the ambient, subtype, and common-box dual cuts. `peierls_contour_count_rayExit_shadow` is the count consumer with `hanchor`, `hshadow`, and ordinary within-`F` connectivity explicit. Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `RayExitShadowRoute.lean` | Ray-exit shadow route |
| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The ray first-exit distance is bounded by the cut size** — `Peierls/RayExitBound.lean`. `firstExit_lt_dartDualCut_card` — the `+e₀`-ray first-exit distance `k` satisfies `k < |dartDualCut F|`, **without** contour connectivity. At the first exit all `ray0 i 0, …, ray0 i k` lie in `F` (`exists_first_exit_below`); from each `ray0 i t` a `+e₁` ray exits `F` (`exists_first_exit_ray1`), giving a boundary dart (`exists_e1_exit_dart`, `tail = q`) with tail `x`-coordinate `i₀ + t` (`exists_tail_at`). These `k+1` darts are distinct (different tail `x`-coordinate), so `k+1 ≤ |BoundaryDart F| = |dartDualCut F|`. This bounds the Peierls ray anchors to the fixed sequence `z_0, …, z_r`, making the contour count **volume-independent**. Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `RayExitBound.lean` | Anchor distance bound `k < r` |
| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The bounded ray anchor** — `Peierls/RayAnchorBound.lean`. `exists_ray_anchor_lt_card` — combining the ray anchor (`exists_ray_anchor_dualCutInBox`) with the first-exit bound (`firstExit_lt_dartDualCut_card`) at a *single* first-exit index `k`: a finite box droplet `F ∋ i` has an anchor `ray0 i k` on its common-box dual cut with `k < |dualCutInBox|` (using `|dualCutInBox| = |dartDualCut|`). This is the input to the contour count's anchor-cover, pinning each droplet to one of the `r` fixed ray anchors `z_0, …, z_{r-1}`. Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `RayAnchorBound.lean` | Bounded ray anchor |
| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The ray anchor set** — `Peierls/RayAnchorSet.lean`. `rayAnchorSet Λd i r` — the dual-box vertices equal to `ray0 i k` for some `k < r`. `mem_rayAnchorSet` — `⟨ray0 i k, _⟩ ∈ rayAnchorSet` for `k < r`. `rayAnchorSet_card_le` — `|rayAnchorSet| ≤ r` (its image under `Subtype.val` lies in `(range r).image (ray0 i)`). `rayAnchorSet_cover` — every box droplet `F ∋ i` with `|dualCutInBox| = r` has an anchor in `rayAnchorSet` (from `exists_ray_anchor_lt_card`). This supplies the anchor set `Z`, the cover, and `|Z| ≤ r` of `contour_count_le`, yielding `r · 16^r`. Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `RayAnchorSet.lean` | Ray anchor set |
| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The Peierls contour count** — `Peierls/PeierlsContourCount.lean`. `peierls_contour_count` — the number of neighbour-closed, ground-avoiding, **single-orbit** box droplets `S ∋ i` with box edge cut of size `r` is at most `r · (2·2)^{2r} ≤ 32^r`, volume-independently. The counting engine for the Peierls contour bound: a dart orbit of length `k` is a closed walk, so the number of contours of a given length near a fixed vertex is geometric in the length. Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `ClosedWalkCount.lean` | 2D, walk counting |
| **FV §3.7.2 / Issue #3631** | **The low-temperature Peierls tail vanishes** — `Peierls/LowTempTail.lean`. The contour bound gives `µ⁺(σ₀=-1) ≤ ∑_{r≥1} C^r e^{-2βJr} = q/(1-q)` with `q(β) = C·e^{-2βJ}`. `lowTempRate_tendsto_zero` — `C·e^{-2βJ} → 0` as `β → ∞` (for `J > 0`). `peierls_low_temp_tail_tendsto_zero` — hence `q/(1-q) → 0` as `β → ∞`. This is the analytic input to `m*(β)>0`: the opposite-spin probability is squeezed to `0` (the high-temperature counterpart took the `n→∞` box limit; here the limit is `β→∞`). Reference: Friedli–Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), §3.7.2, pp. 109–116. | `LowTempTail.lean` | Analysis, capstone tail |
| `eta_nonneg_finite_vol` (§17.7) | `η ≥ 0` | `PhaseTransition.lean` | Finite |

**Done (liminf form, PR #1643)**: infinite-volume lift of Prop 5.4.2
via `Filter.liminf` of the per-stage `+`-Gibbs expectation. The
canonical ∞-vol `+`-BC quantity
`plusGibbsExpectationLiminf G Λ ⟨J, 0, β⟩ B (fun n σ => sign(σ iₙ))`
satisfies the genuine infinite-volume Peierls bound:
`0 ≤ 1 − plusGibbsExpectationLiminf ≤ exp(-c·β)` under the same
per-stage hypotheses as `prop_5_4_2_along_exhaustion`. Theorems
`prop_5_4_2_plusGibbsExpectationLiminf_lower_bound`,
`prop_5_4_2_plusGibbsExpectationLiminf_bound` (upper),
`prop_5_4_2_plusGibbsExpectationLiminf` (full sandwich) in
`PeierlsInfinite.lean`. The full Gibbs-measure projective-limit
construction with canonical `B` and `i` from the ambient geometry
is deferred (would require additional ambient-geometry machinery
beyond this lift).

## Axioms

**No declared axioms remain anywhere in the project** (modulo Mathlib):
`cor_4_3_3_scaled` (PR #3912) and `phi4_single_site_nonneg` (PR #3917) made GJ
§4.3 axiom-free, and the three §17.8 axioms behind `η ≤ 1` —
`ball_boundary_tight_infinite`, `shellSup_contraction`, and
`polynomialDecay_contraction_factor_tendsto` — are now all proven theorems
(`TheoremEtaLe1/`), so GJ §17.8 Theorem 17.8.1 is unconditional.

`polynomialDecay_contraction_factor_tendsto` (the last declared axiom) was
**discharged as a theorem** in `TheoremEtaLe1/Contraction.lean`: the boundary edge
count obeys the *surface* bound `|latticeBallBoundaryEdges d r| ≤ 2d·|sphere_r| =
O(r^{d-1})` (`latticeBallBoundaryEdges_card_le_sphere` + `latticeSphere_card_le'`,
the sphere count via the two-to-one last-coordinate projection
`LatticeSphereCard.lean`), each endpoint sits at distance `∈ {r, r+1}` where the
polynomial-decay hypothesis (extracted from the cofinite filter) gives
`corr∞·dist^{d-1} ≤ δ`, and the volume-cancelling product
`O(r^{d-1})·O(r^{-(d-1)})·δ ≤ C·δ` is driven below any `ε`.

`shellSup_contraction` was **discharged as a theorem** in the same file: it is
the shell supremum of `ball_boundary_tight_infinite`, proved by `ciSup_le` over
the distance shell, translation invariance
(`correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_vaddFinset_of_translationInvariant`), and the
triangle shell bound `|y−l| ≥ |y|−(r+1)` (boundary endpoints have distance
`≤ r+1`). The corrected `1 ≤ r` hypothesis (inherited from
`ball_boundary_tight_infinite`) is threaded through the contraction-factor,
high-temperature mass-gap, η≤1, and cubic-shell consumers.

`ball_boundary_tight_infinite` was **discharged as a theorem** in
`TheoremEtaLe1/BallBoundaryInfinite.lean` (infinite-volume limit of the
finite-stage `ball_boundary_simon_lieb_tight`). The formalization found the
original axiom statement false for `r = 0` (the origin lies on every boundary
edge, and the `{0,0}` Finset collapses to `⟨σ₀⟩ = 0`) and for
`latticeDistance d 0 x = r + 1` (the sink lies on a boundary edge); the proved
theorem carries the corrected hypotheses `1 ≤ r` and
`r + 1 < latticeDistance d 0 x`. The distance condition is already supplied by
the downstream `shellSup_contraction` (shell points at distance `≥ r + 2`); the
radius condition `1 ≤ r` is genuinely new and must be threaded into
`shellSup_contraction` when it is itself discharged.

The discharged GHS-corollary family (Issue #3906):
- ~~`lebowitz_third`~~: **deleted in PR #3910** — false as stated (decoupling `i` with `h > 0` forces `⟨σⱼσₖ⟩ ≤ ⟨σⱼ⟩⟨σₖ⟩`, contradicting strict GKS-II); replaced by the proven `Lebowitz.cor_4_3_4`, which is exactly `u₃ ≤ 0` (GHS) at general `h ≥ 0`
- ~~`lebowitz_four`~~: **deleted in PR #3909** — false as stated (its `h = 0` specialisation `U₄ ≤ −2⟨σᵢσⱼ⟩⟨σₖσₗ⟩` is refuted by two disjoint strongly coupled edges); replaced by the proven `Lebowitz.lebowitz_four_zero_field`
- ~~`lebowitz_inductive`~~: **discharged in PR #3911** (true as stated) — replaced by the proven `Lebowitz.lebowitz_inductive_bound` (GJ Cor 4.3.5 intermediate bound, p. 62)

| §4.4 / FV Thm 3.21 | **General FKG for arbitrary monotone observables** (nonnegativity hypothesis removed) | **Done (3 linearity lemmas + main theorem)** | `Inequalities/FKGGeneral.lean`. `fkg_ising` (inheriting Mathlib `fkg`'s interface) requires `0 ≤ f`, `0 ≤ g`; the genuine FV Theorem 3.21 holds for **any** monotone `f, g` of arbitrary sign. `fkg_ising_of_monotone`: for ferromagnetic `p` and monotone nondecreasing `f, g : Config ι → ℝ`, `⟨f⟩⟨g⟩ ≤ ⟨fg⟩` — no nonnegativity assumption. Proof by covariance shift-invariance: the Gibbs covariance `⟨fg⟩ − ⟨f⟩⟨g⟩` is unchanged under adding constants to `f, g` (constant terms cancel by linearity + normalisation `⟨1⟩ = 1`); subtracting the finite minima `a = min f`, `b = min g` gives nonnegative monotone `f' = f − a ≥ 0`, `g' = g − b ≥ 0` with the same covariance, and `fkg_ising` applied to `f', g'` closes it (`nlinarith`). Supporting Gibbs-expectation linearity lemmas `gibbsExpectation_const` (`⟨c⟩ = c`), `gibbsExpectation_add` (`⟨F+H⟩ = ⟨F⟩+⟨H⟩`), `gibbsExpectation_const_mul` (`⟨cF⟩ = c⟨F⟩`) are proved alongside. |

The nine duplicated proofs of `gibbsExpectation_*` (FKGGeneral), `gibbsExpectationJ_*` (FKGInhomogeneous), and `gibbsExpectationBC_*` (FKGBoundaryCondition) now delegate to these helpers (single source of truth; faster builds). Public lemma names/signatures unchanged. |

FV Theorem 3.21 allows a **collection of nonnegative couplings** `J = (J_{ij})` (one per edge) and an **arbitrary field** `h`, not just the uniform scalar `IsingParams.J`. New inhomogeneous Gibbs stack: `interactionEnergyJ` (`-∑_e J(e)·s(σ_i)s(σ_j)`), `hamiltonianJ`, `boltzmannWeightJ` (`exp(-βH)`), `boltzmannWeightJ_pos`, `partitionFunctionJ` (+`_pos`/`_ne_zero`), `gibbsExpectationJ` (+linearity `_const`/`_add`/`_const_mul`). Key lattice condition `boltzmannWeightJ_log_supermodular`: for `β ≥ 0` and `J(e) ≥ 0` (field `h` **arbitrary** — its term is modular), `w(σ)w(σ') ≤ w(σ⊔σ')w(σ⊓σ')`; per-edge supermodularity (`spin_edge_supermodularJ`, 16-case) summed with nonnegative weights `J(e)`. FKG theorems: `fkg_isingJ` (nonnegative monotone `f,g`, via Mathlib `fkg`) and `fkg_isingJ_of_monotone` (**arbitrary**-sign monotone `f,g`, via covariance shift). This matches FV 3.21 exactly for the free-boundary case (nonnegative per-edge `J`, arbitrary `h`); arbitrary boundary conditions remain follow-up (#3558). |

Completes FV Theorem 3.21 in full generality (nonnegative inhomogeneous `J`, arbitrary field `h`, **arbitrary boundary condition** `η`). The boundary-condition Gibbs measure is the inhomogeneous Boltzmann weight (#3559) **conditioned** on configurations agreeing with `η` outside `Λ` — no new Hamiltonian, since the boundary interactions are already in `boltzmannWeightJ`. Key insight: the set `{σ \| agreesOff Λ η σ}` is a **sublattice** (`agreesOff_sup`/`agreesOff_inf`: off `Λ` both equal `η i`, so `⊔`/`⊓` stay `η i` via `sup_idem`/`inf_idem`), so `boltzmannWeightBC := Set.indicator {σ \| agreesOff Λ η σ} boltzmannWeightJ` is again log-supermodular (`boltzmannWeightBC_log_supermodular`: agreeing case = inhomogeneous log-supermodularity, disagreeing case = `0 ≤` nonneg). `partitionFunctionBC` (`+_pos` via `η` itself in the conditioned set), `gibbsExpectationBC` (`+_const`/`_add`/`_const_mul`). FKG theorems `fkg_isingBC` (nonnegative) and `fkg_isingBC_of_monotone` (arbitrary-sign monotone, via covariance shift). With #3559 this realizes the complete FV 3.21 statement (collection of nonnegative couplings + arbitrary `h` + arbitrary boundary condition). |
| §4.1 / FV §3.6.2 | **Field monotonicity of the Gibbs expectation** (Holley) | **Done (cross-supermodularity + 2 monotonicity theorems)** | `Inequalities/MonotonicityField.lean`. Increasing the external field `h` increases the Gibbs expectation of every monotone observable: `h ≤ h' ⟹ ⟨φ⟩_h ≤ ⟨φ⟩_{h'}` for nondecreasing `φ`. Foundational for the stochastic ordering of Ising measures, the `±` extremal states, and the infinite-volume limit. Proved via Mathlib's **`holley`** (`Combinatorics.SetFamily.FourFunctions`): the two normalised Boltzmann weights at fields `h ≤ h'` satisfy the Holley domination condition `boltzmannWeight_field_cross_supermodular`: `w_h(a)·w_{h'}(b) ≤ w_h(a⊓b)·w_{h'}(a⊔b)` — interaction part = edge log-supermodularity (`spin_edge_supermodular_F`, weight `βJ ≥ 0`); field part = per-site `field_site_mono` (`h·s(a)+h'·s(b) ≤ h·s(a⊓b)+h'·s(a⊔b)` for `h ≤ h'`, weight `β ≥ 0`). `gibbsExpectation_field_mono_of_nonneg` (nonnegative `φ`, via `holley` on the normalised measures) and `gibbsExpectation_field_mono` (**arbitrary** monotone `φ`, via the constant shift since `⟨φ⟩_h ≤ ⟨φ⟩_{h'}` is shift-invariant). |
| FV §3.6.2 / §6 | **Boundary-condition monotonicity** (Holley) | **Done (cross-supermodularity + 2 monotonicity theorems)** | `Inequalities/MonotonicityBoundary.lean`. Raising the boundary condition raises the Gibbs expectation of every monotone observable: `η ≤ η' ⟹ ⟨φ⟩^η_Λ ≤ ⟨φ⟩^{η'}_Λ` for nondecreasing `φ`. **Cornerstone of the extremal `±` Gibbs states and the infinite-volume limit** (the `+` boundary gives the maximal state, the `−` the minimal). Proved via Mathlib's `holley` on the conditioned boundary-condition weights (#3560). The order-aware conditioning closure is the key: `agreesOff_inf_of_le`/`agreesOff_sup_of_le` — if `a` agrees with `η` off `Λ` and `b` with `η'`, then (since `η ≤ η'`) `a⊓b` agrees with `η` (`η⊓η'=η`) and `a⊔b` agrees with `η'` (`η⊔η'=η'`). Hence `boltzmannWeightBC_cross_supermodular`: `w^η(a)·w^{η'}(b) ≤ w^η(a⊓b)·w^{η'}(a⊔b)` (agreeing case = `boltzmannWeightJ_log_supermodular`, else `0 ≤` nonneg). `gibbsExpectationBC_boundary_mono_of_nonneg` (nonnegative `φ`) and `gibbsExpectationBC_boundary_mono` (arbitrary monotone `φ`, via constant shift). |
| FV §6 | **Extremal `±` boundary states + magnetization ordering** | **Done (extremal configs + bracketing + magnetization sandwich)** | `Inequalities/MonotonicityExtremal.lean`. The boundary-condition monotonicity (#3562) is sharpest at the extremal configurations `plusConfig` (all up, maximal) and `minusConfig` (all down, minimal): `le_plusConfig`/`minusConfig_le` (`σ ≤ plusConfig`, `minusConfig ≤ σ` via `Spin.le_up`/`Spin.down_le`). For any boundary condition `η` and monotone `φ`, `gibbsExpectationBC_extremal_sandwich`: `⟨φ⟩^−_Λ ≤ ⟨φ⟩^η_Λ ≤ ⟨φ⟩^+_Λ` — the `±` boundary conditions bracket all boundary conditions — at this finite volume the `+` boundary condition gives the largest expectation of every monotone observable, the `−` the smallest (the foundation for the extremal infinite-volume `±` Gibbs states constructed as thermodynamic limits). Concrete application: `spin_sign_monotone` (`Spin.sign ℝ` monotone) + `singleSpinObs_monotone` (`σ ↦ s(σ_i)` monotone) give `magnetizationBC_extremal_sandwich`: the local magnetization `⟨σ_i⟩^η_Λ` is squeezed between the `±` states. A finite-volume bracketing, foundational for the extremal infinite-volume `±` states. |
| FV Lemma 3.22 | **Volume monotonicity of the `+` state** (conditioning + FKG) | **Done (shell indicator + weight identity + antitone theorem)** | `Inequalities/VolumeMonotonicity.lean`. The `+` boundary expectation of a monotone observable **decreases as the volume grows**: `Λ₁ ⊆ Λ₂ ⟹ ⟨φ⟩^+_{Λ₂} ≤ ⟨φ⟩^+_{Λ₁}` (`gibbsExpectationBC_plus_volume_antitone`). With the dual `−`-state bound this exhibits the `±` states as **monotone limits over an exhaustion** — the construction of the extremal infinite-volume Gibbs states (the project's central goal). Proof by the conditioning structure: the `Λ₁` `+` state is the `Λ₂` `+` state conditioned on the shell `Λ₂∖Λ₁` being all `+` (`agreesOff_plus_iff_shell`: `agreesOff Λ₁ + = (+ on shell) ∧ agreesOff Λ₂ +`). The shell event is an **up-set**, so its indicator `upShellIndicator` is monotone (`upShellIndicator_monotone`), and the weight identity `boltzmannWeightBC_plus_eq_shell_mul` (`w^+_{Λ₁} = 1_A·w^+_{Λ₂}`) gives `⟨φ·1_A⟩^+_{Λ₂} = ⟨φ⟩^+_{Λ₁}·⟨1_A⟩^+_{Λ₂}`; the FKG inequality `⟨φ·1_A⟩ ≥ ⟨φ⟩⟨1_A⟩` (`fkg_isingBC_of_monotone`, both monotone) then yields `⟨φ⟩^+_{Λ₂} ≤ ⟨φ⟩^+_{Λ₁}` after cancelling `⟨1_A⟩^+_{Λ₂} > 0`. |

| §3.4 / Issue #3565 | **★ The cubic-exhaustion `+`-state functional on ℤ^d (towards FV Thm 3.17) ★** | **Done (functional + same-support linearity + positivity + normalisation; sequence-independence / translation-invariance / `−` state / cross-support union are follow-up)** | `Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/LocalObservableState.lean`. The **monotone-difference decomposition** (the elementary role of FV Lemma 3.19): `LocalObservable.upper` (`K·rank + φ`) and `lower` (`K·rank`), `K = 2·max|φ|`, both monotone (the large `K·rank` dominates `φ`'s variation across any covering step), with `phi_eq_upper_sub_lower` (`φ = upper − lower`). `plusBoxObsExpectation` — the `+` box expectation of an arbitrary observable, with `plusBoxObsExpectation_{eq_sub,add,const_mul,const,mono}` (linearity from `gibbsExpectationBC_add`/`const_mul`/`const`). `plusStateExpectation` — the infinite-volume `+`-state functional (the difference of the two monotone limits), with `tendsto_plusStateExpectation` (the screened box expectations converge to it). The functional is **linear** (`plusStateExpectation_add`, `_const_mul`, *same support*), **normalised** (`plusStateExpectation_const` = `c`), **positive** (`plusStateExpectation_nonneg`), **monotone** (`plusStateExpectation_mono`), and **consistent** with the monotone-observable limit (`plusStateExpectation_of_monotone` = `⨅`). All via `tendsto_nhds_unique` / `le_of_tendsto`. (Sequence independence, translation invariance, the `−` state, and cross-support union linearity are follow-up before the full FV Thm 3.17 `+` state.) |

| §5.1 | Cluster property — conditional decay: summable ⇒ cofinite → 0 (pp. 72–74) | **Done (conditional real-analysis step)** | `truncated2Infinite_tendsto_cofinite_zero_of_summable` (`AmbientLattice.lean`): `Summable (fun j : V => truncated2Infinite G Λ p i j) → Tendsto ... Filter.cofinite (nhds 0)`. The `Summable` hypothesis is a finiteness condition on the two-point function summed over `j`; in translation-invariant / connected-correlation settings it matches the physical "finite susceptibility" (away from the critical line). `Filter.cofinite` is the filter of cofinite subsets; on `Fin d → ℤ` (with `d ≥ 1`) bounded subsets are finite, so cofinite aligns with the informal "|r| → ∞" filter. Direct specialization of mathlib's `Summable.tendsto_cofinite_zero`. ℤ^d wrapper `truncated2Infinite_latticeGraph_tendsto_cofinite_zero_of_summable` (`Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CorrelationDecay.lean`). This PR supplies the elementary real-analysis building block; later Simon–Lieb/high-temperature results discharge the summability input in high-temperature regimes. (PR #779.) |
| §5.1 | ℓ¹ lattice distance on ℤ^d (infrastructure for cluster decay) | **Done (definition + 5 basic lemmas)** | `latticeDistance (d : ℕ) (x y : Fin d → ℤ) : ℕ := ∑ i, (x i - y i).natAbs` (`Lattice.lean`). Basic lemmas: `latticeDistance_self` (`= 0`), `latticeDistance_comm` (symmetry), `latticeDistance_eq_zero_iff` (`= 0 ↔ x = y`), `latticeDistance_triangle` (`d(x,z) ≤ d(x,y) + d(y,z)`), and `latticeGraph_adj_iff_latticeDistance_eq_one` (`(latticeGraph d).Adj x y ↔ latticeDistance d x y = 1`). Range kept in `ℕ` to sidestep `ℕ`/`ℤ`/`ℝ` cast bookkeeping in subsequent summability arguments. Part of the §5.1 cluster-decay infrastructure series (Epic #780); the companion statement that `Filter.cofinite` on `Fin d → ℤ` is equivalent to `latticeDistance (fixed basepoint, ·) → ∞` for `d ≥ 1` (which upgrades PR #779 into a concrete distance-based statement) is deferred to a follow-up PR. (PR #781.) **Graph distance = ℓ¹ distance**: `latticeGraph_dist_eq_latticeDistance` (`(latticeGraph d).dist x y = latticeDistance d x y`) — the shortest-path metric of the lattice graph coincides with the ℓ¹ distance, with `latticeGraph_connected` (ℤ^d is connected), `latticeDistance_exists_adj_step` (the inductive geodesic step: one coordinate moved toward `y` reduces the distance by one), `latticeGraph_exists_walk_length` (a geodesic walk of length `latticeDistance` exists, giving `dist ≤`), and `latticeDistance_le_walk_length` (every walk has length `≥ latticeDistance`, giving `dist ≥`). This grounds the lattice-distance decay statements in the actual graph metric. |
| §5.1 | Finite ℓ¹ balls + proper map to ℕ (infrastructure for cluster decay) | **Done (finite balls + `Tendsto` to `atTop` along `cofinite`)** | `latticeDistance_le_finite` + `tendsto_latticeDistance_atTop_cofinite` (`Lattice.lean`). The ball `{j : Fin d → ℤ | latticeDistance d i j ≤ N}` is finite for every dimension `d`, basepoint `i`, and radius `N`, via the coordinatewise bound `(i k - j k).natAbs ≤ latticeDistance d i j` (one summand is at most a ℕ-sum) placing each `j k` in a finite integer interval `[i k - N, i k + N]`, then `Set.Finite.pi` + `Set.finite_Icc`. The proper-map property `Tendsto (fun j => latticeDistance d i j) Filter.cofinite Filter.atTop` follows by reducing `Filter.eventually_cofinite` to finiteness of `{j | latticeDistance d i j < N}` for every `N`, a subset of the ball at radius `N`. No `d ≥ 1` hypothesis (for `d = 0` the domain `Fin 0 → ℤ` is a singleton, `Filter.cofinite` collapses to `⊥`, and the Tendsto holds vacuously). Combined with PR #779's conditional cofinite cluster decay this is the upgrade pathway to a distance-based "`U_2 → 0` as `d_latt(i,j) → ∞`" statement. (PR #782.) |
| §17.1 | 1D Ising transfer matrix — eigenpairs, trace, determinant, tanh ratio (Issue #3511 PR 1) | **Done (definition + 11 lemmas)** | `isingTransferMatrix1D (a : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ := Matrix.of (fun i j => Real.exp (a · spin1D i · spin1D j))` (`TransferMatrix/OneDim.lean`), the zero-field 1D Ising transfer matrix `T(a)ᵢⱼ = e^{a·sᵢ·sⱼ}` with `a = βJ` and spin values `spin1D = ![1, -1]`, explicitly `T(a) = !![eᵃ, e⁻ᵃ; e⁻ᵃ, eᵃ]` — the concrete instance of the Glimm–Jaffe §17.1 transfer-matrix method. Entry lemmas (`isingTransferMatrix1D_{zero_zero,zero_one,one_zero,one_one}`), symmetry `Tᵀ = T` (`isingTransferMatrix1D_transpose`), entrywise positivity (`isingTransferMatrix1D_pos`). Eigenvalues `transferEigenvalueTop a = eᵃ + e⁻ᵃ = 2 cosh a` (`transferEigenvalueTop_eq`, `transferEigenvalueTop_pos`) and `transferEigenvalueBot a = eᵃ − e⁻ᵃ = 2 sinh a` (`transferEigenvalueBot_eq`); trace `= 2eᵃ = λ₊ + λ₋` (`trace_isingTransferMatrix1D`) and determinant `= e²ᵃ − e⁻²ᵃ = λ₊·λ₋` (`det_isingTransferMatrix1D`). Hadamard-basis eigenpairs `T·(1,1) = λ₊·(1,1)` (`isingTransferMatrix1D_mulVec_hadamardTop`) and `T·(1,−1) = λ₋·(1,−1)` (`isingTransferMatrix1D_mulVec_hadamardBot`). Spectral ratio `λ₋/λ₊ = tanh a` (`transferEigenvalue_ratio`) — the source of the ferromagnetic 1D correlation decay rate `−log tanh a` (`a = βJ > 0`; GJ §17.5). First PR of the transfer-matrix formalization programme (Issue #3511); next: cyclic-chain partition function as a trace `Z_N = Tr(Tᴺ)`. |
| §17.1 | 1D transfer matrix diagonalization — `Tr(Tᴺ) = λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ` (Issue #3511 PR 2) | **Done (definition + 13 lemmas)** | `TransferMatrix/OneDimPower.lean`. Hadamard matrix `hadamardMatrix = !![1, 1; 1, −1]` with `H·H = 2·1` (`hadamardMatrix_mul_self`), `det H = −2` (`hadamardMatrix_det`, unit `hadamardMatrix_isUnit_det`), inverse `H⁻¹ = (1/2)·H` (`hadamardMatrix_inv`). Eigenvalue diagonal `transferDiagonal a = diagonal ![λ₊, λ₋]` (entry simp lemmas `transferDiagonal_{zero_zero,one_one,zero_one,one_zero}`). The inverse-free **Hadamard intertwining** `T(a)·H = H·D(a)` (`isingTransferMatrix1D_mul_hadamard`) powers by induction to `T(a)ᴺ·H = H·D(a)ᴺ` (`isingTransferMatrix1D_pow_mul_hadamard`), giving the diagonalization `T(a)ᴺ = H·D(a)ᴺ·H⁻¹` (`isingTransferMatrix1D_pow_eq_conj`) with `D(a)ᴺ = diagonal ![λ₊ᴺ, λ₋ᴺ]` (`transferDiagonal_pow`). Hence the **cyclic-chain partition function** `Tr(T(a)ᴺ) = λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ` (`trace_isingTransferMatrix1D_pow`, via `trace_mul_comm` + `H⁻¹·H = 1`) and `det(T(a)ᴺ) = (λ₊·λ₋)ᴺ` (`det_isingTransferMatrix1D_pow`). The trace `Z_N = λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ` is (for physical `N ≥ 1`) the partition function of the `N`-site cyclic Ising chain at zero field; the identity is a pure algebraic fact valid for all `N : ℕ` (GJ §17.1). Issue #3511 PR 2; next: the configuration-sum = trace identity `∑_σ ∏ exp(βJ σᵢσᵢ₊₁) = Tr(Tᴺ)` and the exact two-point function `⟨σ₀σₙ⟩ = (tanh βJ)ⁿ`. |
| §17.1 | 1D Ising log-partition (free-energy) density `log(2 cosh βJ)` from transfer matrix (Issue #3511 PR 3) | **Done (8 lemmas)** | `TransferMatrix/OneDimFreeEnergy.lean`. Builds on the trace formula `Tr(Tᴺ) = λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ` (#3513) to derive the per-site log-partition (dimensionless free-energy) density `(1/N)·log Z_N` of the 1D Ising chain. Spectral-gap inputs for `a = βJ > 0`: `transferEigenvalueBot_pos` (`λ₋ = 2 sinh a > 0`), `transferEigenvalueBot_lt_top` (`λ₋ < λ₊`, gap `2e⁻ᵃ`, all `a`), `transferEigenvalue_ratio_pos`/`transferEigenvalue_ratio_lt_one` (`λ₋/λ₊ = tanh a ∈ (0,1)`), and `tendsto_transferEigenvalue_ratio_pow` (`(λ₋/λ₊)ᴺ → 0`). Main limit `tendsto_log_eigenvalueSum_div_nat`: `(1/N)·log(λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ) → log λ₊` (writing `λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ = λ₊ᴺ(1 + tanhᴺ a)`, the subdominant eigenvalue gives the vanishing correction `(1/N)·log(1 + tanhᴺ a) → 0`). Trace corollary `tendsto_log_trace_pow_div_nat`: `(1/N)·log Tr(Tᴺ) → log λ₊`; since `Z_N = Tr(Tᴺ)` (cyclic chain), this is the 1D Ising log-partition density (free energy `f = −β⁻¹·log(2 cosh βJ)`). Closed form `log_transferEigenvalueTop_eq`: `log λ₊ = log(2 cosh a)`. The transfer-matrix solution of the 1D Ising free energy `f = −β⁻¹ log(2 cosh βJ)` (GJ §17.1). Issue #3511 PR 3. |
| §17.1 | Closed-walk trace identity `Tr(Mᴺ)=∑ paths` for matrix powers (Issue #3511 PR 4) | **Done (6 declarations)** | `TransferMatrix/TraceSum.lean`. The combinatorial core of the transfer-matrix partition function `Z_N = Tr(Tᴺ)`, for any finite matrix `M : Matrix ι ι R` over a commutative semiring (Mathlib has no such lemma; only `adjMatrix_pow_apply_eq_card_walk` for 0/1 matrices). `pathWeight M σ := ∏_{i:Fin n} M (σ i.castSucc) (σ i.succ)` (open-path edge product) with `pathWeight_snoc` (`pathWeight (snoc σ x) = pathWeight σ · M (σ last) x`). **Open-path entry formula** `pow_apply_eq_sum`: `(Mⁿ) a b = ∑_{σ:Fin(n+1)→ι} [σ 0 = a ∧ σ (last n) = b] · pathWeight M σ`, by induction peeling the last edge via `Fin.snocEquiv`. **Closed-walk trace identity** `trace_pow_eq_sum`: `Tr(Mⁿ) = ∑_{σ:Fin(n+1)→ι} [σ 0 = σ (last n)] · pathWeight M σ` (sum over vertex sequences returning to their start), from `pow_apply_eq_sum` on the diagonal. Cyclic vocabulary `closedWalkWeight M σ := ∏_{i:Fin n} M (σ i) (σ (i+1))` (cyclic `Fin n`, `NeZero n`) with the factorization `closedWalkWeight_succ`: `closedWalkWeight τ = pathWeight τ · M (τ last) (τ 0)`. Underlies the cyclic 1D Ising `Z_N = Tr(Tᴺ)` (GJ §17.1). Issue #3511 PR 4; next: `partitionFunction (cycleGraph N) = Tr(Tᴺ) = λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ` and `⟨σ₀σₙ⟩ = (tanh βJ)ⁿ`. |
| §17.1 | Cyclic trace identity `Tr(Tᴺ)=∑ closed walks` and 1D Ising `Z_N=λ₊ᴺ+λ₋ᴺ` (Issue #3511 PR 5) | **Done (5 declarations)** | `TransferMatrix/{TraceSum,TraceSum1D}.lean`. Completes the closed-walk identity (#3515) into its purely cyclic form. `pathWeight_eq_closedWalkWeight_init`: for a vertex sequence returning to its start (`σ 0 = σ (last (m+1))`), `pathWeight M σ = closedWalkWeight M (init σ)`. **Cyclic trace identity** `trace_pow_eq_sum_cycle`: `Tr(M^(m+1)) = ∑_{τ:Fin(m+1)→ι} closedWalkWeight M τ`, reindexing the open-return form `trace_pow_eq_sum` by the `init`/`snoc` bijection (`Finset.sum_bij'`) between vertex sequences returning to their start and closed walks. 1D Ising specialization (`TraceSum1D.lean`): `trace_isingTransferMatrix1D_pow_eq_sum_cycle` (`Tr(T(a)^(m+1)) = ∑_{σ:Fin(m+1)→Fin 2} closedWalkWeight T(a) σ`) and the headline `sum_closedWalkWeight_isingTransferMatrix1D`: `∑_{σ:Fin(m+1)→Fin 2} closedWalkWeight T(a) σ = λ₊^(m+1) + λ₋^(m+1)` — the transfer-matrix evaluation `Z_N = Tr(Tᴺ) = λ₊ᴺ + λ₋ᴺ` of the cyclic N-site zero-field Ising chain (GJ §17.1). Issue #3511 PR 5; next: connecting `closedWalkWeight` to the project's `partitionFunction (cycleGraph N)` Hamiltonian form, and `⟨σ₀σₙ⟩ = (tanh βJ)ⁿ`. |
| §17.1 | 1D Ising two-point function (transfer-matrix ratio) `→ (tanh βJ)ⁿ` (Issue #3511 PR 6) | **Done (14 declarations)** | `TransferMatrix/OneDimTwoPoint.lean`. The transfer-matrix expression for the two-point function, `Tr(S·Tⁿ·S·T^{N-n})/Tr(Tᴺ)` (its identification with the Gibbs `⟨σ₀σₙ⟩` via the cyclic config sum is a later PR), with spin operator `spinOperator = diag(1,−1)` and `swapMatrix P = !![0,1;1,0]`. **Key**: the spin operator swaps the Hadamard eigenvectors, `spinOperator_mul_hadamard` (`S·H = H·P`), so `hadamardInv_mul_spinOperator_mul_hadamard` (`H⁻¹·S·H = P`) and `swapMatrix_mul_transferDiagonal_pow_mul_swapMatrix` (`P·D(a)ᵏ·P = diagonal ![λ₋ᵏ, λ₊ᵏ]`). **Two-point trace** `twoPointTrace`: `Tr(S·Tⁿ·S·Tᵐ) = λ₋ⁿ·λ₊ᵐ + λ₊ⁿ·λ₋ᵐ` (via `spinOperator_mul_pow`, `S·Tⁿ = H·P·D(a)ⁿ·H⁻¹`). | §17.1 | **1D Ising transfer matrix with external field `h ≠ 0` — foundations** (Issue #3538 PR 1) | **Done (definition + ~21 declarations)** | `TransferMatrix/OneDimField.lean`. Extends the zero-field 1D transfer matrix (#3512) to a **general external field**: `isingTransferMatrix1DField (a b : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ := Matrix.of (fun i j => exp (a·sᵢ·sⱼ + (b/2)(sᵢ+sⱼ)))` with `a = βJ`, `b = βh`, explicitly `T(a,b) = !![e^{a+b}, e^{-a}; e^{-a}, e^{a-b}]`. Entry lemmas (`isingTransferMatrix1DField_{zero_zero,zero_one,one_zero,one_one}`), symmetry `Tᵀ = T` (`isingTransferMatrix1DField_transpose`), entrywise positivity (`isingTransferMatrix1DField_pos`). **Discriminant** `fieldTransferDiscriminant a b = e^{2a} sinh²b + e^{-2a}` with `fieldTransferDiscriminant_pos` (`> 0`, real distinct eigenvalues). **Eigenvalues** `fieldTransferEigenvalue{Top,Bot} a b = eᵃ cosh b ± √D`; trace `2 eᵃ cosh b` (`trace_isingTransferMatrix1DField`) and determinant `e^{2a} − e^{-2a}` (`det_isingTransferMatrix1DField`). Unlike `h = 0`, the eigenvectors are not the fixed Hadamard pair, so the spectral data is organised via the **characteristic polynomial**: Vieta sum `λ+ + λ- = trace` (`fieldTransferEigenvalueTop_add_bot{,_eq_trace}`), product `λ+ · λ- = det` (`fieldTransferEigenvalueTop_mul_bot{,_eq_det}`, using `√D² = D` and `cosh²b = sinh²b + 1`), and the characteristic equation `λ± ² = trace·λ± − det` (`fieldTransferEigenvalue{Top,Bot}_sq`). Ordering `λ- < λ+` (`fieldTransferEigenvalueBot_lt_top`), positivity `0 < λ+` (`fieldTransferEigenvalueTop_pos`) and `0 < λ-` for `a > 0` (`fieldTransferEigenvalueBot_pos`, via `λ+ · λ- = e^{2a} − e^{-2a} > 0`). **Zero-field bridge** at `b = 0`: `isingTransferMatrix1DField_zero` (`= isingTransferMatrix1D a`), `fieldTransferDiscriminant_zero` (`= e^{-2a}`), `fieldTransferEigenvalue{Top,Bot}_zero` (`= transferEigenvalue{Top,Bot} a`). The foundational PR of the general external-field 1D transfer-matrix programme (Glimm–Jaffe §17.1); next: partition function `Z_N = λ+ᴺ + λ-ᴺ`, free energy, magnetization `m(h)`, susceptibility `∂_h m`. Issue #3538 PR 1. |

Issue #3538 PR 2; next: magnetization `m(h)`, susceptibility `∂_h m`. |
| §17.1 | **1D Ising field magnetization `m(h) = sinh βh / √(sinh²βh + e^{-4βJ})`** (Issue #3538 PR 3) | **Done (6 declarations)** | `TransferMatrix/OneDimFieldMagnetization.lean`. The magnetization of the 1D Ising chain in a field as the field-derivative of the free-energy density `log λ₊` (#3540). `fieldMagnetization a b = sinh b / √(sinh²b + e^{-4a})` (`a = βJ`, `b = βh`). Helper `sqrt_fieldTransferDiscriminant`: `√D = eᵃ √(sinh²b + e^{-4a})` (from `D = e^{2a}(sinh²b + e^{-4a})`, `√(e^{2a}) = eᵃ`). `hasDerivAt_fieldTransferDiscriminant` (`∂_b D = e^{2a}·2 sinh b cosh b`). **Headline** `hasDerivAt_log_fieldTransferEigenvalueTop`: `d/db [log λ₊(a,b)] = fieldMagnetization a b` — the logarithmic derivative `(∂_b λ₊)/λ₊` collapses to `sinh b/√(...)` via the discriminant factorisation (built from `HasDerivAt.sqrt`, `Real.hasDerivAt_cosh`, `HasDerivAt.log`). Physics: `fieldMagnetization_zero` (`m(a,0) = 0` — no spontaneous magnetization in 1D) and `abs_fieldMagnetization_lt_one` (`|m| < 1` strictly sub-saturated, since `√(sinh²b + e^{-4a}) > |sinh b|` as the field gap `e^{-4a} > 0`). The exact 1D Ising magnetization curve (GJ §17.1). Issue #3538 PR 3; next: susceptibility `∂_h m`. |
| §17.1 | **1D Ising field susceptibility `χ = ∂_b m = cosh βh·e^{-4βJ}/(sinh²βh+e^{-4βJ})^{3/2}`** (Issue #3538 PR 4) | **Done (5 declarations)** | `TransferMatrix/OneDimFieldSusceptibility.lean`. The susceptibility of the 1D Ising chain in a field as the field-derivative of the magnetization (#3541). `fieldSusceptibility a b = cosh b·e^{-4a}/((sinh²b+e^{-4a})·√(sinh²b+e^{-4a}))` (`a = βJ`, `b = βh`), strictly positive (`fieldSusceptibility_pos`). **Headline** `hasDerivAt_fieldMagnetization`: `d/db [fieldMagnetization a b] = fieldSusceptibility a b` — by the quotient rule (`HasDerivAt.div`) on `m = sinh b/√X` (`X = sinh²b + e^{-4a}`), the derivative collapses via `(√X)² = X`, `X − sinh²b = e^{-4a}` (substituting `e^{-4a} = q² − sinh²b`, `q = √X`, then `field_simp`). **Physical susceptibility** `hasDerivAt_fieldMagnetization_field`: `∂_h m = β·χ` (chain rule through `b = βh`). **Zero-field bridge** `fieldSusceptibility_zero`: `χ(a,0) = e^{2a}` (so `∂_h m|₀ = β e^{2a}` — the gap-enhanced zero-field susceptibility of the 1D chain). Completes the exact solution of the 1D Ising chain in a field (matrix → eigenvalues → partition function → free energy → magnetization → susceptibility); GJ §17.1. Issue #3538 PR 4 (final). |
| §17.1 | **General finite layer transfer matrix and trace identities** (Issue #3511) | **Done (finite layer abstraction)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerTransfer.lean`. Adds the finite-state layer abstraction needed before the higher-dimensional hyperplane transfer-matrix route. For a finite layer state space `Ω`, one-layer weight `u : Ω → R`, and transition weight `k : Ω → Ω → R`, `layerTransferMatrix u k : Matrix Ω Ω R` is defined by `T a b = u b * k a b`. `layerClosedWalkWeight_eq_prod` identifies the induced cyclic weight with `∏ i, u(c(i+1)) * k(c i)(c(i+1))`. **Headline** `layerTransferPartition_trace` specialises the existing closed-walk identity to layers: `layerTransferPartitionTrace u k (m+1) = ∑ c : Fin(m+1) → Ω, layerClosedWalkWeight u k c`; `layerTransferPartition_trace_eq_sum_prod` gives the product-expanded version. Marked insertion wrappers `layerTransferOnePointTrace_eq_sum`, `layerMarkedClosedWalkWeight`, `layerTransferCorrelation_matrixElement_eq_sum_markedClosedWalk`, `layerMarkedClosedWalkWeight_eq_prod`, and `layerTransferCorrelation_matrixElement_eq_sum_prod` package `Tr(D_f T^n)` and `Tr(D_f T^a D_f T^b)` for later finite-volume hyperplane two-point representations; the layer wrapper hides the redundant `NeZero (a+b)` requirement behind `hb : 0 < b`. This PR deliberately contains no spectral gap, Perron--Frobenius argument, lattice hyperplane identification, thermodynamic limit, or exponential-decay theorem; those remain later #3511 steps. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306. |

Positivity lemmas `layerCyclicGibbsWeight_pos` and `layerCyclicPartition_pos` package the strictly-positive finite-volume case. The two-insertion side defines `layerMarkedCyclicGibbsWeight`, `layerTwoPointNumerator`, and the normalised `layerTwoPoint`; **headline** `layerTwoPoint_eq_trace_ratio` identifies the normalised Gibbs two-point function with `Tr(D_f T^a D_f T^b) / Tr(T^(a+b))`. The hyperplane-facing entry points `LayerState S := Config S`, `layerSpinAt`, `layerSpinTwoPoint`, and `layerSpinTwoPoint_eq_trace_ratio` specialise the observable to a spin at a fixed transverse site, ready for a later finite box/hyperplane edge decomposition. This remains finite and abstract: no concrete `Z^d` box decomposition, Perron--Frobenius theory, thermodynamic limit, or exponential-decay estimate. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306. |

| §17.1 | **Two-site interacting layer spectral data** (Issue #3511) | **Done (explicit interacting transverse-edge diagonalization)** | `TransferMatrix/TwoSiteInteractingLayerSpectralData.lean`. Constructs the first *interacting* transverse-edge layer transfer matrix and its explicit orthogonal diagonalization, the first case the free Walsh route cannot diagonalize. The layer is `S = Fin 2` with internal graph `completeGraph (Fin 2)` (one transverse edge) and identity longitudinal transition; `layerInternalWeight_completeGraph_fin2` and `layerSymmetricTransferMatrix_fin2_complete_eq_reindex_twoSiteInteracting` identify the balanced layer matrix with the explicit `4×4` matrix `twoSiteInteractingTransferMatrix`. The even spin sector mixes the two constant/antidiagonal modes through a square-root rotation: with `A = e^{3a}+e^{-a}`, `B = e^{a}+e^{-3a}`, `Δ = A−B`, `rad = √(Δ²+16)`, the rotation `c = √((rad+Δ)/(2 rad))`, `s = √((rad−Δ)/(2 rad))` satisfies `c²+s²=1`, `c·s·rad=2`, and the eigenvector identities `c·(rad−Δ)=4 s`, `s·(rad+Δ)=4 c` (`twoSiteK2_rotC_mul`, `twoSiteK2_rotS_mul`, proved by squaring and the nonnegativity of both sides). The four eigenvalues are `top, evenBot = (A+B ± rad)/2`, `flipOdd = e^{3a}−e^{-a}`, `swapOdd = e^{a}−e^{-3a}` (`twoSiteInteractingTransferEigenvalue`). `twoSiteInteractingChangeOfBasis` is orthogonal in both directions, the columns are eigenvectors (`twoSiteInteractingTransferMatrix_mul_changeOfBasis`), and `twoSiteInteractingTransferMatrix_diagonalizes` packages `M = Q diag(λ) Qᵀ`, yielding `RealOrthogonalSpectralData` for both the abstract matrix (`twoSiteInteractingTransferOrthogonalSpectralData`) and the physical zero-field layer (`twoSiteInteractingLayerOrthogonalSpectralData`). This file only packages explicit finite spectral data; it does not prove simple spectrum, signed positivity, the open-boundary decay discharge, a thermodynamic limit, or final hyperplane decay. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |

The four eigenvalues are strictly ordered `top > flipOdd > swapOdd > evenBot > 0` for `0 < βJ`: `twoSiteK2Top_gt_FlipOdd` (via `rad ≥ Δ`), `twoSiteK2FlipOdd_gt_SwapOdd` (via `flipOdd = e^{2a}·swapOdd`), and the determinant relation `twoSiteK2_det` (`top·evenBot = flipOdd·swapOdd`, from `rad²=Δ²+16` and `e^{3a}e^{-3a}=e^{a}e^{-a}=1`) give `twoSiteK2EvenBot_pos` and `twoSiteK2SwapOdd_gt_EvenBot`. Hence `twoSiteInteractingTransferOrthogonalSpectralData_simpleSpectrum` and its physical-layer wrapper `twoSiteInteractingLayerOrthogonalSpectralData_simpleSpectrum`. The dominant rotation column `(c,s,s,c)/√2` is strictly positive (`twoSiteK2RotC_pos`, `twoSiteK2RotS_pos` from `rad > |Δ|`), giving signed-positive top columns for the abstract matrix and the physical layer. The decay parameter `twoSiteInteractingTheta = flipOdd/top` satisfies `theta < 1` (`twoSiteInteractingTheta_lt_one`) and `theta · top = flipOdd`, and the spectral window `twoSiteInteractingLayerSpectralWindow_theta` bounds every non-top eigenvalue by `theta · top` in absolute value. This file supplies the `SimpleSpectrum`, signed-positive, and subdominant-window inputs; the open boundary-window cap and the open-slab decay discharge are a later step (the interacting balanced boundary vector is not constant, so the cap argument differs from the one-site/free cases). It does not prove the open-slab decay bound, a thermodynamic limit, or final hyperplane decay. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Two-site interacting open boundary-window discharge** (Issue #3511) | **Done (first interacting transverse-edge open-slab decay)** | `TransferMatrix/TwoSiteInteractingLayerOpenBoundaryWindow.lean`. Completes the interacting `K2` open-boundary discharge, the first unconditional finite open-slab same-transverse-site decay for a genuinely interacting transverse-edge layer. The balanced boundary vector `v(ω) = sqrt(internalWeight ω) = exp((βJ/2)·s(ω0)s(ω1))` is not constant but is flip-even (`twoSiteInteractingLayer_boundaryVector_flip_even`); the two odd rotation columns are `ColumnFlipOdd` (`twoSiteInteractingLayer_flipOdd_columnFlipOdd`, `..._swapOdd_columnFlipOdd`), so their boundary coordinates vanish (`boundaryCoordinates_zero_of_equiv_even_odd`). Only the even-bottom coordinate survives, so by Parseval (`sum_boundaryCoordinates_sq`) the off-top boundary mass is `vectorSqNorm − coord_top²` (`twoSiteInteractingLayer_boundaryCoordinateRestSq_eq`). The explicit top coordinate `√2(c·e^{βJ/2}+s·e^{-βJ/2})` (`twoSiteInteractingLayer_boundaryCoordinates_top`) and `vectorSqNorm = 2(e^{βJ}+e^{-βJ})` satisfy `vectorSqNorm ≤ 2·coord_top²` (the difference reduces to `(Δ·sinh(βJ)+4)/rad > 0` via the rotation identities and `Δ > 0` for `βJ > 0`), so the off-top mass is at most `coord_top²`, the boundary-window cap is `1`, and it strictly exceeds `theta` (`twoSiteInteractingLayer_theta_lt_cap`). Feeding the #4060 simple-spectrum / signed-positive / spectral-window inputs and the #4057 `columnSimpleEigenspaces_of_simpleSpectrum` bridge through `correlation_layerOpenSlabGraph_abs_le_of_signedPositiveSimpleParity_boundaryWindow`, `correlation_twoSiteInteractingLayerOpenSlabGraph_abs_le_of_simpleSpectrum` gives the unconditional finite interacting open-slab bound in prefactor form with decay parameter `theta = flipOdd/top` for `0 < βJ`. It does not prove a closed-form decay rate, a thermodynamic limit, or final hyperplane decay. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Two-site interacting open strip mass decay** (Issue #3511) | **Done (mass-form interacting open-slab decay)** | `TransferMatrix/TwoSiteInteractingLayerOpenDecay.lean`. The decay parameter `twoSiteInteractingTheta a = flipOdd/top` is positive (`twoSiteInteractingTheta_pos`) and strictly below `1`, so the decay mass `twoSiteInteractingMass a = -log(twoSiteInteractingTheta a) = log(top/flipOdd)` (`twoSiteInteractingMass_eq_log_top_div_flipOdd`) is positive (`twoSiteInteractingMass_pos`), and `twoSiteInteractingTheta a ^ n = exp(-(twoSiteInteractingMass a)·n)` (`twoSiteInteractingTheta_pow_eq_exp_neg_mass`, via `Real.exp_log` and `Real.exp_nat_mul`). This is finite: it does not prove a closed-form rate beyond `-log θ`, a thermodynamic limit, or final hyperplane decay. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
