Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Quadratic-form spectral gap for the explicit subdominant ratio** (Issue #3511) | **Done (Rayleigh-gap reduction of the second-eigenvalue bound)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormGap.lean`. Reduces the explicit subdominant ratio bound to a **quadratic-form gap** on the subspace orthogonal to the maximal spectral column, using only the existing orthogonal-diagonalization API (no Courant--Fischer). `RealOrthogonalSpectralData.spectralCoord_changeOfBasis_column_ne` (non-maximal columns are orthonormal, from `orthogonal_left`), `eigenvalue_abs_le_of_quadraticForm_gap` (`(∀ v with spectralCoord v top = 0, \|⟨v,Mv⟩\| ≤ ρ·‖v‖²) → ∀ i ≠ top, \|λ_i\| ≤ ρ`; proved by applying the gap to the `i`-th unit spectral column whose quadratic form is `λ_i`), and `subdominantAbsRatio_maxEigenIndex_le_of_quadraticForm_gap` (`(0 ≤ θ) ∧ (∀ v with spectralCoord v maxEigenIndex = 0, \|⟨v,Mv⟩\| ≤ θ·λ_max·‖v‖²) → subdominantAbsRatio ≤ θ`, composing with the #4067 hook). Layer wrappers `finiteTransverseHermitianExplicitRatio_le_of_quadraticForm_gap` and `cubicLayerHermitianExplicitRatio_le_of_quadraticForm_gap`. This converts the transverse-volume-uniform target from an eigenvalue list into a single Rayleigh bound on the top-orthogonal subspace — what a later Dobrushin/Hilbert-metric estimate must produce. Finite and conditional on the quadratic-form gap; does not construct it or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Row-sum Rayleigh bound for the transfer-matrix quadratic form** (Issue #3511) | **Done (unconditional Schur/Gershgorin-type Rayleigh bound)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormRowSum.lean`. An unconditional Rayleigh bound for the quadratic form of a symmetric matrix in terms of its maximal absolute row sum (a discrete Schur-test / Gershgorin estimate by direct double-sum expansion + AM--GM, no operator-norm machinery): `matrixAbsRowSum M i := ∑ j \|M i j\|`, `matrixMaxAbsRowSum`, `matrixAbsRowSum_le_matrixMaxAbsRowSum`, `vectorSqNorm_nonneg`, and the core `abs_matrixQuadraticForm_le_of_absRowSum_le_of_symmetric` (`Mᵀ = M ∧ (∀ i, ∑ j \|M i j\| ≤ C) → \|⟨v,Mv⟩\| ≤ C·‖v‖²`; proof `\|∑ᵢⱼ vᵢMᵢⱼvⱼ\| ≤ ∑ᵢⱼ\|Mᵢⱼ\|\|vᵢ\|\|vⱼ\| ≤ ∑ᵢⱼ\|Mᵢⱼ\|(vᵢ²+vⱼ²)/2 = ∑ᵢ rowSumᵢ·vᵢ² ≤ C·‖v‖²`, folding the column sum into the row sum via symmetry) with corollary `abs_matrixQuadraticForm_le_matrixMaxAbsRowSum_mul_vectorSqNorm`. The hook `RealOrthogonalSpectralData.subdominantAbsRatio_maxEigenIndex_le_of_matrixMaxAbsRowSum_le` (`0 ≤ θ ∧ matrixMaxAbsRowSum M ≤ θ·λ_max → subdominantAbsRatio ≤ θ`) feeds this into the #4068 quadratic-form-gap hook. The bound holds for all vectors so it bounds the top eigenvalue too and does not by itself give a strict gap; a later off-diagonal-mass splitting on the top-orthogonal subspace will. Finite and unconditional; does not construct a strict spectral gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Off-diagonal split of the transfer-matrix quadratic form** (Issue #3511) | **Done (diagonal-separated Gershgorin bound)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormOffDiag.lean`. Refines the row-sum Rayleigh bound by separating the diagonal: for symmetric `M`, `\|⟨v,Mv⟩ − ∑ i M i i·v i²\| ≤ (max_i ∑_{j≠i}\|M i j\|)·‖v‖²`. The proof reuses #4069's row-sum bound on the **off-diagonal part** `matrixOffDiagPart M := fun i j => if i = j then 0 else M i j` (diagonal zeroed), avoiding `j≠i` bookkeeping: `matrixOffDiagAbsRowSum`/`matrixMaxOffDiagAbsRowSum`, structural lemmas `matrixOffDiagPart_transpose_eq_self_of_transpose_eq_self` (off-diag part of symmetric is symmetric), `matrixAbsRowSum_matrixOffDiagPart` (its row sum = off-diagonal row sum), `matrixQuadraticForm_offDiagPart_eq_sub_diag` (its quadratic form = QF − diagonal), then the headline `abs_matrixQuadraticForm_sub_diag_le_of_offDiagAbsRowSum_le_of_symmetric` (+ max form) by applying #4069 to `matrixOffDiagPart M`. This is the structural step before the strict gap: on the subspace orthogonal to the entrywise-positive top eigenvector the diagonal and top contributions are subtracted, leaving the off-diagonal mass (later file). Finite and unconditional; does not construct a strict spectral gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Diagonal bounds for the transfer-matrix quadratic form** (Issue #3511) | **Done (two-sided diagonal Rayleigh bounds)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormDiag.lean`. The diagonal companion to the off-diagonal split: the diagonal contribution `∑ i, M i i·v i²` is two-sidedly controlled by the extremal diagonal entries. `matrixMaxDiag`/`matrixMinDiag`/`matrixMaxAbsDiag` (= sup'/inf'/sup' of `\|·\|` of the diagonal) with accessors `matrixDiag_le_matrixMaxDiag`, `matrixMinDiag_le_matrixDiag`, `matrixAbsDiag_le_matrixMaxAbsDiag`, and the bounds `diagQuadraticForm_le_matrixMaxDiag_mul_vectorSqNorm` (`∑ M i i·v i² ≤ max diag·‖v‖²`), `matrixMinDiag_mul_vectorSqNorm_le_diagQuadraticForm` (`min diag·‖v‖² ≤ ∑ M i i·v i²`), and `abs_diagQuadraticForm_le_matrixMaxAbsDiag_mul_vectorSqNorm` (`\|∑ M i i·v i²\| ≤ max\|diag\|·‖v‖²`). Unconditional, requires neither symmetry nor spectral data. Combined with the off-diagonal mass bound (#4070), these subtract the diagonal/top contributions on the top-orthogonal subspace toward a strict gap. Finite and unconditional; does not construct a strict spectral gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Gershgorin Rayleigh envelope for the transfer-matrix quadratic form** (Issue #3511) | **Done (two-sided Gershgorin envelope + ratio hook)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormGershgorin.lean`. Combines the diagonal (#4071) and off-diagonal (#4070) bounds by triangle inequality into a two-sided Gershgorin Rayleigh envelope for symmetric `M` (`offMass := matrixMaxOffDiagAbsRowSum M`): `abs_matrixQuadraticForm_le_matrixMaxAbsDiag_add_matrixMaxOffDiagAbsRowSum_mul_vectorSqNorm` (`\|⟨v,Mv⟩\| ≤ (max\|diag\| + offMass)·‖v‖²`), `matrixQuadraticForm_le_matrixMaxDiag_add_matrixMaxOffDiagAbsRowSum_mul_vectorSqNorm` (upper), `matrixMinDiag_sub_matrixMaxOffDiagAbsRowSum_mul_vectorSqNorm_le_matrixQuadraticForm` (lower), and the hook `RealOrthogonalSpectralData.subdominantAbsRatio_maxEigenIndex_le_of_gershgorinAbsDiagOffDiag_le` (`0 ≤ θ ∧ max\|diag\| + offMass ≤ θ·λ_max → subdominantAbsRatio ≤ θ`) feeding the #4068 quadratic-form-gap hook. The envelope holds for all vectors so it bounds the top eigenvalue too and is NOT by itself a strict spectral gap; it is the Rayleigh form from which the top-eigenvalue contribution is subtracted on the top-orthogonal subspace. Finite and unconditional; does not construct a strict spectral gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Top-column deflation and the strict-gap reduction** (Issue #3511) | **Done (circularity-breaking deflated Gershgorin hook)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormDeflation.lean`. The all-vector Gershgorin envelope cannot give a strict gap (it bounds the top eigenvalue too). This file deflates the top eigenpair: `RealOrthogonalSpectralData.matrixTopDeflation E top := fun i j => M i j − λ_top·(changeOfBasis i top · changeOfBasis j top)` (`= M − λ_top·w_top w_topᵀ` with `w_top` the maximal spectral column). It is symmetric (`matrixTopDeflation_transpose_eq_self`), its quadratic form differs from `M`'s by exactly the top contribution (`matrixQuadraticForm_sub_topDeflation`: `⟨v,Mv⟩ − ⟨v,(deflated)v⟩ = λ_top·(spectralCoord v top)²`, proved via `Fintype.sum_mul_sum`), hence agrees with `M` on the top-orthogonal subspace (`matrixQuadraticForm_eq_topDeflation_of_spectralCoord_eq_zero`). The headline hook `subdominantAbsRatio_maxEigenIndex_le_of_topDeflatedGershgorin_le` (`0 ≤ θ ∧ maxAbsDiag(deflated) + maxOffDiagAbsRowSum(deflated) ≤ θ·λ_max → subdominantAbsRatio ≤ θ`) applies the #4072 envelope to the **deflated** matrix and feeds the #4068 gap, **breaking the circularity**: the hypothesis is the deflated matrix's entrywise Gershgorin quantity (with the dominant eigenvalue removed), not the second eigenvalue. This reduces the strict gap to controlling the deflated entries — i.e. the top eigenvector concretely (a later quantitative Perron/Dobrushin estimate). Finite and conditional; does not construct a strict gap unconditionally or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Entries and annihilation identity of the top deflation** (Issue #3511) | **Done (deflated-entry accessors + annihilation)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerQuadraticFormDeflationEntries.lean`. Exposes the entrywise structure of the top deflation and the defining annihilation identity. `RealOrthogonalSpectralData.matrixTopDeflation_apply` (`= M i j − λ_top·(w_i·w_j)`), `matrixTopDeflation_diag` (`= M i i − λ_top·w_i²`), `matrixTopDeflation_offDiagAbsRowSum` (`= ∑_{j≠i} \|M i j − λ_top·w_i w_j\|`) reduce the deflated Gershgorin quantity (which controls the strict gap via #4073) to explicit expressions in `M`'s entries and the top eigenvector components `w_x = changeOfBasis x top`. The annihilation identity `matrixTopDeflation_mulVec_column_eq_zero` (`(deflated)·w_top = 0`, from the eigen-equation `M·w_top = λ_top·w_top` and unit norm `∑ x w_x² = 1`) confirms the maximal eigenvalue is removed, isolating the genuinely remaining task — a quantitative entrywise bound on `λ_top·w_i w_j` (a Perron--Frobenius / Hilbert-metric estimate) for a later file. Finite, unconditional algebraic identities; does not bound the deflated entries quantitatively, construct a strict gap, or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Doob (Perron) stochastic normalization of the transfer matrix** (Issue #3511) | **Done (row-stochastic conjugation)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerDoobTransform.lean`. For a positive matrix `M` with a strictly positive right eigenvector `w` of eigenvalue `λ > 0` (the Perron eigenpair), the Doob transform `matrixDoobTransform M λ w i j := M i j·w j/(λ·w i)` is an entrywise positive, row-stochastic matrix similar to `M/λ`. `matrixDoobTransform_apply`, `matrixDoobTransform_pos` (entrywise positive when `M` positive, `w` positive, `λ > 0`), `matrixDoobTransform_row_sum` (`∑ j P i j = 1`, from `∑ j M i j w j = λ w i`), and `matrixDoobTransform_mulVec` (it conjugates eigenvectors: `M·v = μ·v → P·(v/w) = (μ/λ)·(v/w)`). This is the structural reduction underlying a future quantitative Perron--Frobenius / Dobrushin estimate: the spectral gap of `M` becomes the gap of the stochastic `P`, controlled by a Dobrushin / Hilbert-projective-metric contraction coefficient (not proved here). Finite algebraic identities for an abstract positive Perron eigenpair; does not prove a quantitative contraction, a strict gap, or a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Dobrushin oscillation contraction for row-stochastic matrices** (Issue #3511) | **Done (the contraction estimate)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerDobrushinContraction.lean`. The central Dobrushin contraction: a row-stochastic matrix `P` contracts the oscillation `vectorOscillation v = max_i v_i − min_i v_i` by its Dobrushin coefficient `matrixDobrushinCoefficient P = ½·max_{i,i'} ∑_j \|P i j − P i' j\|`: `vectorOscillation_mulVec_le_dobrushin` (`osc(P·v) ≤ δ(P)·osc(v)`, for `∀ i ∑_j P i j = 1`). Proved via the constant-shift `c = (max v + min v)/2`: `(Pv)_i − (Pv)_{i'} = ∑_j (P i j − P i' j)(v_j − c)` (using `∑_j(P i j − P i' j) = 0`), bounded by `∑_j \|P i j − P i' j\|·(osc/2) ≤ 2δ·(osc/2) = δ·osc`. Supporting: `MatrixRowStochastic`, `vectorOscillation_nonneg`/`_const`, `vectorOscillation_le_of_forall_sub_le`, `abs_sub_midpoint_le_half_oscillation`, `matrixDobrushinRowDistance`/`Coefficient` (+ `_nonneg`, `matrixDobrushinRowDistance_le_coefficient`, `sum_abs_row_sub_le_two_dobrushin`), and `matrixDoobTransform_rowStochastic` connecting it to the Doob normalization. The eigenvalue corollary (#4077): `sub_le_vectorOscillation`, `vectorOscillation_smul_le` / `vectorOscillation_smul` (`osc(μ·v) = \|μ\|·osc(v)`), `abs_eigenvalue_le_dobrushin_of_mulVec` (a nonconstant eigenvector of a row-sum-one matrix has `\|μ\| ≤ δ(P)`), and `abs_eigenvalue_div_le_dobrushin_doob_of_mulVec` (for `M` with positive Perron eigenpair `(λ,w)`, any eigenvalue `μ` with nonconstant `v/w` satisfies `\|μ/λ\| ≤ δ(Doob)`). This is the route to the spectral gap: the second eigenvalue of the stochastic Doob matrix is bounded by `δ`, so a uniform `δ < 1` yields a uniform gap (the quantitative `δ < 1` from the layer entries is a later file). Finite, unconditional; does not bound `δ` quantitatively, prove a strict gap, or a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Doeblin minorization and a strict Dobrushin bound** (Issue #3511) | **Done (δ < 1 for positive stochastic matrices)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerDoeblin.lean`. Bounds the Dobrushin coefficient below `1` by the Doeblin mass `matrixDoeblinMass P = ∑_j min_i P i j`: `matrixColMin` (column minimum), `abs_sub_eq_add_sub_two_mul_min` (`\|a−b\| = a+b−2 min a b`), `matrixDobrushinRowDistance_eq_one_sub_sum_min` (`½∑_j\|P i j−P i' j\| = 1−∑_j min(P i j,P i' j)` for row-stochastic P), and the headline `matrixDobrushinCoefficient_le_one_sub_doeblinMass` (`δ(P) ≤ 1 − ∑_j min_i P i j`). For an entrywise positive stochastic matrix the Doeblin mass is positive (`matrixDoeblinMass_pos_of_entrywisePositive`), so `matrixDobrushinCoefficient_lt_one_of_entrywisePositive_rowStochastic` gives `δ(P) < 1`, specialized to the Doob transform by `matrixDobrushinCoefficient_matrixDoobTransform_lt_one`. With the eigenvalue bound (#4077) this gives a strict second-eigenvalue gap for the stochastic Doob matrix. The bound is not yet uniform in the transverse box size: a uniform high-temperature lower bound on the Doob entries (the quantitative Perron-vector estimate) is a later file. Finite, unconditional; does not give a transverse-volume-uniform gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Subdominant ratio bounded by the Doob Dobrushin coefficient** (Issue #3511) | **Done (abstract strict-gap capstone)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerDoobSpectralGap.lean`. Ties the abstract spectral-gap machinery end-to-end: the explicit subdominant absolute ratio of a real orthogonally diagonalized entrywise positive matrix is bounded by the Dobrushin coefficient of its Doob transform, hence strictly below one. `exists_eq_const_of_vectorOscillation_eq_zero` (zero oscillation ⇒ constant), the crux `vectorOscillation_div_signedPositiveColumn_ne_zero` (for `i ≠ top`, `v_i/w_top` is nonconstant — else `v_i = c·w_top` contradicts the orthonormality `changeOfBasis_columns_not_smul`), the headline `RealOrthogonalSpectralData.subdominantAbsRatio_maxEigenIndex_le_dobrushin_doob` (`subdominantAbsRatio ≤ δ(Doob)`, by feeding `\|λ_i/λ_top\| ≤ δ(Doob)` (#4077) into the #4067 hook), and `subdominantAbsRatio_maxEigenIndex_lt_one_via_doob` (`< 1`, composing with the strict Doeblin bound `δ(Doob) < 1` of #4078). This is an alternative, abstract proof of the strict subdominant bound, expressed through `δ(Doob)` — the quantity a later high-temperature estimate makes uniform in the transverse box size; the bound here is not uniform. Finite, unconditional; does not give a transverse-volume-uniform gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Projective cross-ratio and its row/column scaling invariance** (Issue #3511) | **Done (route-independent Hilbert-metric scaffolding)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerProjectiveDiameter.lean`. The Hilbert projective (Birkhoff) metric route is governed by the projective cross-ratio `matrixProjectiveCrossRatio A i j a b = (A i a·A j b)/(A i b·A j a)`. The defining invariance `matrixProjectiveCrossRatio_rowColScale` (scaling `A i j ↦ r i·A i j·c j` by positive row/column factors leaves the cross-ratio unchanged) yields two cancellations isolating the gap-controlling quantity from the unknown Perron data: `matrixProjectiveCrossRatio_layerSymmetricTransferMatrix` (the balanced `M a b = √(u a)·k a b·√(u b)` has the cross-ratio of the bare kernel `k` — the `√u` cancel) and `matrixProjectiveCrossRatio_matrixDoobTransform` (the Doob transform `M i j·w j/(λ·w i)` has the cross-ratio of `M` — `w`,`λ` cancel), composed in `matrixProjectiveCrossRatio_matrixDoobTransform_layerSymmetricTransferMatrix` (Doob of the balanced matrix has the cross-ratio of `k` alone, independent of both `u` and the Perron vector `w`). This is route-independent infrastructure for any later Hilbert-metric / Birkhoff--Hopf contraction argument; the contraction theorem `δ ≤ tanh(Δ/4)` and the (subtle, tensorized) uniform high-temperature estimate are not proved here, and the raw global projective diameter is not claimed uniformly small. Finite algebraic identities; does not bound the Dobrushin coefficient, give a transverse-volume-uniform gap, or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Site factorization of the identity-transition projective cross-ratio** (Issue #3511) | **Done (site-additive log cross-ratio; obstruction made explicit)** | `TransferMatrix/LayerIdentityTransitionProjective.lean`. The identity-transition layer kernel factorizes over transverse sites (`layerTransitionWeight_identity_eq_exp_sum`: `k ω η = exp(βJ ∑_x s(ω x)·s(η x))`), so its projective cross-ratio is a single exponential of a **sum over sites**: `matrixProjectiveCrossRatio_layerTransitionWeight_identity` gives `cr(k;ω,ω',η,η') = exp(βJ ∑_x (s(ω x)−s(ω' x))·(s(η x)−s(η' x)))`. By the #4080 scaling invariance, the Doob transform of the balanced **cubic** transfer matrix has the same cross-ratio (`matrixProjectiveCrossRatio_doob_cubic_identity_eq_exp_sum`) — site-additive, independent of both the layer weight `u` and the Perron vector `w`. This makes the Hilbert-metric structure explicit: the log cross-ratio is additive over transverse sites (each contributing at most `4·\|βJ\|`), so the *global* projective diameter grows linearly in the number of transverse sites — precisely why a transverse-volume-uniform gap cannot come from the global Dobrushin/diameter bound alone; a uniform estimate must exploit the site-tensorized structure (a local/tensorized contraction, a later research arc). Finite algebraic identities; does not give a transverse-volume-uniform gap or prove a thermodynamic limit. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 | **Finite free-layer Walsh open flip-parity route** (Issue #3511) | **Done (finite free-layer open certificate)** | `TransferMatrix/FreeLayerWalshSpectralWindow.lean` and `TransferMatrix/FreeLayerWalshOpenPerron.lean`. Supplies the concrete free-layer inputs required by the open-boundary flip-parity route. The Walsh character identity `spinProduct_layerStateFlipEquiv` proves that a Walsh column changes by `(-1) ^ |A|` under global spin flip, giving `freeLayerTransferOrthogonalSpectralData_columnFlipParity` and its physical zero-field wrapper without invoking arbitrary Hermitian spectral-theorem data. The top Walsh column is packaged as signed-positive (`freeLayerTransferOrthogonalSpectralData_top_signedPositiveColumn`, `freeLayerPhysicalOrthogonalSpectralData_top_signedPositiveColumn`). For the free open boundary, `layerOpenBalancedBoundaryVector_bot_h_zero` makes the boundary vector constant `1`, `freeLayerPhysical_boundaryCoordinates_nonTop_zero` shows all non-top Walsh boundary coordinates vanish, and `freeLayerPhysical_boundaryPrefactor_small_tanh` closes the open denominator prefactor condition for `theta = tanh (βJ)`. The constructor `freeLayerOpenMinGapCertificate_tanh` combines these facts with the existing free-layer Walsh subdominant window and the PR #4039 flip-parity constructor, and `correlation_freeLayerOpenSlabGraph_same_transverse_abs_le_tanh` exposes the resulting finite open-slab same-transverse-site bound. This is finite and free-layer only: it does not prove an interacting cubic-layer spectral window, a thermodynamic limit, or final hyperplane exponential decay. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 / §17.5 | **Finite free-layer Walsh open sharp prefactor** (Issue #3511) | **Done (finite free-layer coefficient-one decay)** | `TransferMatrix/FreeLayerWalshOpenDecay.lean`. Sharpens the finite free-layer open estimate by eliminating the remaining open spectral prefactor ratio. The singleton Walsh index `freeLayerWalshSingleton` has down-spin set `{x}`, and `layerSpinAt_eq_spinProduct_singleton` identifies a fixed-site spin with that singleton Walsh character. The column identity `freeLayerPhysical_top_column_mul_layerSpinAt` and orthogonality give `freeLayerPhysical_markedMatrix_layerSpinAt_top_eq_ite` and its symmetric form: the marked matrix sends the top Walsh mode only to the singleton mode. Since the free open boundary has only the top coordinate, `freeLayerPhysical_boundarySpectralPartitionPrefactor_eq_top_sq` and `freeLayerPhysical_boundaryMarkedSpectralPrefactor_eq_top_sq` prove that the denominator and marked numerator prefactors are the same top-coordinate square; `freeLayerPhysical_openPrefactorRatio_eq_one` packages their ratio as `1`. The consumer `correlation_freeLayerOpenSlabGraph_same_transverse_abs_le_tanh_clean` gives the clean finite open bound `|<σ_(left,x) σ_(left+sep,x)>| ≤ tanh(βJ)^sep`, and `correlation_freeLayerOpenSlabGraph_same_transverse_abs_le_exp_neg_mass` rewrites it using `correlationMass`. This is finite and free-layer only: it does not prove an interacting cubic-layer spectral window, a thermodynamic-limit bridge, or final hyperplane decay. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 / §17.5 | **Free-layer open cubic-box transport bridge** (Issue #3511) | **Done (finite free-layer axis-graph transport)** | `TransferMatrix/FreeLayerWalshOpenInfiniteVolume.lean`. Adds the finite geometric bridge needed before lifting the free-layer open estimate toward ambient finite volumes. The new `freeLayerAxisGraph` is the longitudinal-only graph on `Z^(d+1)`: adjacent vertices differ by one in the first coordinate and agree in all transverse coordinates. The embedding `freeLayerOpenSlabCubicBoxEquiv` sends a `2N`-step open free-layer slab over `cubicBox d N` to the ambient cubic box `cubicBox (d+1) N` by `(i,x) ↦ (i-N,x)`. The graph identity `freeLayerOpenSlabGraph_map_cubicBoxEquiv` proves that the transported finite open free-layer slab is exactly `Ambient.inducedGraph (freeLayerAxisGraph d) (Ambient.cubicBox (d+1) N)`. The correlation transport theorem `correlation_induced_freeLayerAxisGraph_cubicBox_eq_openSlab`, its absolute-value form, and `abs_correlation_induced_freeLayerAxisGraph_cubicBox_le_of_openSlab` move finite open-slab estimates onto the induced cubic-box finite volume. This is deliberately a free-layer axis-graph bridge only: it does not claim decay for the full `latticeGraph (d+1)` with transverse edges, does not prove an interacting spectral window, and does not complete the thermodynamic-limit step. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 / §17.5 | **Finite free-layer axis-graph cubic-box decay consumer** (Issue #3511) | **Done (finite zero-field axis-graph cubic-box decay)** | `TransferMatrix/FreeLayerWalshOpenAxisDecay.lean`. Consumes the sharp finite free-layer open estimate from `FreeLayerWalshOpenDecay.lean` together with the cubic-box transport bridge from `FreeLayerWalshOpenInfiniteVolume.lean`. The two-point definitions `freeLayerOpenCubicSlabTwoPoint` and `freeLayerOpenCubicAxisTwoPoint` select the centre layer and the layer at longitudinal separation `sep` in the `2N`-step slab, assuming `sep ≤ N`, and then transport that observable to the induced finite volume of `freeLayerAxisGraph`. The finite wrappers `correlation_freeLayerOpenSlabGraph_cubicBox_same_transverse_abs_le_tanh_clean` and `correlation_freeLayerOpenSlabGraph_cubicBox_same_transverse_abs_le_exp_neg_mass` specialize the clean open-slab theorem with `left = N` and `right = N - sep`; a private length-cast helper handles the equality `N + sep + (N - sep) = 2N`. The induced consumers `correlation_induced_freeLayerAxisGraph_cubicBox_same_transverse_abs_le_tanh_clean` and `correlation_induced_freeLayerAxisGraph_cubicBox_same_transverse_abs_le_exp_neg_mass` give the corresponding finite cubic-box bounds on `Ambient.inducedGraph (freeLayerAxisGraph d) (Ambient.cubicBox (d+1) N)`. This remains finite, zero-field, and longitudinal-axis only: it does not prove decay for the full cubic lattice with transverse edges, an interacting spectral window, or a thermodynamic-limit theorem. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.1, pp. 304--306; §17.5, pp. 311--312. |
| §17.1 / §17.5 | **Free-layer axis-graph cubic-exhaustion infinite-volume decay** (Issue #3511) | **Done (axis-graph cubic-exhaustion limit)** | `TransferMatrix/FreeLayerWalshOpenAxisInfiniteVolume.lean`. | §5.1 / §18 | **Neighbour-vertex Simon-Lieb transfer kernel** (random-walk representation, Issue #3543 PR 1) | **Done (7 declarations)** | `Inequalities/SimonLiebKernel.lean`. Recasts the edge-sum Simon-Lieb inequality (`correlation_inducedGraph_simon_lieb`) into a reusable **neighbour-vertex transfer kernel** form, the foundation of the random-walk representation of the two-point function (FFS Ch 12, GJ §18). `simonLiebKernel G Λ p j u = if u = j then 1 else ⟨σ_u σ_j⟩` (the `u = j` value `1 = ⟨σ_∅⟩` collects the diagonal-edge `{i,j} △ {i,j} = ∅` contribution); basic properties `simonLiebKernel_{self,of_ne,nonneg,le_one}` (nonneg via GKS-I, ≤ 1 via `abs_correlation_le_one`). Per-edge identity `correlation_symmDiff_eq_simonLiebKernel`: for an edge `e` incident to `i` with other endpoint `u`, `⟨σ^{{i,j} △ toFinset e}⟩ = K(j, u)` (`u = j` → `∅` → 1; `u ≠ j` → `{i,j} △ {i,u} = {u,j}` via `symmDiff_pair_pair_of_ne`). **Headline** `correlation_inducedGraph_simon_lieb_neighbor`: `⟨σ_i σ_j⟩ ≤ βJ ∑_{u ∈ neighborFinset i} K(j, u)` for ferromagnetic `⟨J,0,β⟩`, `i ≠ j` — the one-step transfer form, reindexing the incident-edge sum to a neighbour-vertex sum via `Finset.sum_bij'` + `Sym2.Mem.other` / `Sym2.other_spec`. Iterating this kernel yields the random-walk bound `⟨σ_i σ_j⟩ ≤ ∑_{walks i→j} (βJ)^{length}` (later PRs). Issue #3543 PR 1; next: walk-weight framework + iteration. |
| §5.1 / §18 | **Walk-weight and fixed-length walk-sum framework** (random-walk representation, Issue #3543 PR 2) | **Done (6 declarations)** | `Inequalities/WalkSum.lean`. The combinatorial walk-sum framework underlying the random-walk bound (FFS Ch 12, GJ §18). `walkWeight z w = z^{w.length}` and `walkSum G z i j n = ∑_{w : length-n walk i→j} z^{length}` (`z = βJ` in the Ising application). `walkSum_eq_pow_mul_card`: every length-`n` walk has weight `z^n`, so `walkSum = z^n · #{length-n walks}`. `walkSum_eq_pow_mul_adjMatrix_pow`: `walkSum = z^n · (A^n)_{ij}` (`A` = adjacency matrix, via `adjMatrix_pow_apply_eq_card_walk`). `walkSum_nonneg` (`z ≥ 0`), `walkSum_zero` (`= if i=j then 1 else 0`, the diagonal length-0 walk). **Headline** `walkSum_succ` (neighbour recurrence): `walkSum z i j (n+1) = z · ∑_{u ∈ neighborFinset i} walkSum z u j n` — a length-`(n+1)` walk first steps to a neighbour, then is a length-`n` walk, via the adjacency-matrix identity `(A·A^n)_{ij} = ∑_{u∼i} (A^n)_{uj}` (`adjMatrix_mul_apply`). This recurrence mirrors the one-step Simon-Lieb transfer kernel (#3544); iterating the kernel against it (next PR) yields the random-walk bound `⟨σ_i σ_j⟩ ≤ ∑_{walks i→j} (βJ)^{length}`. Issue #3543 PR 2; next: kernel-to-walk iteration. |
| §5.1 / §18 | **Iterated Simon-Lieb transfer kernel** (random-walk representation, Issue #3543 PR 3) | **Done (5 declarations)** | `Inequalities/SimonLiebIterate.lean`. Iterates the one-step neighbour-vertex Simon-Lieb kernel (#3544) `n` times. `simonLiebIterate p j n i` (recursion on `n`): base `= K(j,i)`, step `simonLiebIterate p j (n+1) i = if i=j then 1 else βJ·∑_{u∼i} simonLiebIterate p j n u` — the `n`-step transfer applied to the kernel, with the diagonal `K(j,j)=1` absorbed at the target `j` (a walk reaching `j` stops, contributing the `⟨σ_∅⟩=1` factor); unfold lemmas `simonLiebIterate_{zero,succ}`. **Headline** `simonLiebKernel_le_simonLiebIterate`: `K(j,i) ≤ simonLiebIterate ⟨J,0,β⟩ j n i` for all `n, i` (induction on `n` generalizing `i`: base reflexivity; `i=j` both sides `1`; `i≠j` combines the one-step kernel `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩ ≤ βJ ∑_{u∼i} K(j,u)` with the induction hypothesis via `βJ ≥ 0` and `Finset.sum_le_sum`). Two-point corollary `correlation_inducedGraph_le_simonLiebIterate`: `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩ ≤ simonLiebIterate ⟨J,0,β⟩ j n i` for `i ≠ j`. | §5.1 / §18 | **High-temperature uniform bound on the iterated Simon-Lieb kernel** (random-walk representation, Issue #3543 PR 4) | **Done (2 declarations)** | `Inequalities/SimonLiebIterateHighTemp.lean`. This is the boundedness input for the random-walk representation — the iterated upper bound for `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩` does not blow up as the number of transfer steps grows (the prerequisite for the first-passage walk-sum limit). | §5.1 / §18 | **Exponential decay of the two-point function via Simon-Lieb iteration** (random-walk representation, Issue #3543 PR 5) | **Done (2 declarations)** | `Inequalities/SimonLiebIterateDecay.lean`. The random-walk (Simon-Lieb) derivation of high-temperature correlation decay from the iterated kernel (#3546). **Distance-localised geometric bound** `simonLiebIterate_le_pow_of_lt_dist`: if the target `j` is more than `n` graph-steps from `i` (`n < dist i j`), then `simonLiebIterate ⟨J,0,β⟩ j n i ≤ (βJ·D)^n` (`D` = degree bound) — the `n`-step transfer never reaches the absorbing diagonal `K(j,j)=1`, so every branch decays geometrically. Induction on `n`: base `0 < dist i j` (kernel `K(j,i) ≤ 1`); step `dist i j > n+1` forces `i ≠ j`, and every neighbour `u ∼ i` still has `dist u j > n` (the edge moves the distance by at most one, `Adj.diff_dist_adj`), so the IH bounds each branch by `(βJ·D)^n`, and summing over `≤ D` neighbours times `βJ` gives `(βJ·D)^{n+1}`. **Headline** `correlation_inducedGraph_le_pow_dist`: for reachable distinct `i, j` (`0 < dist i j`), `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩ ≤ (βJ·D)^{dist(i,j)−1}` (specialising `n = dist−1`, composing with `correlation_inducedGraph_le_simonLiebIterate`) — exponential decay in the graph distance, tending to `0` in the high-temperature regime `βJ·D < 1`. Issue #3543 PR 5; next: ℤ^d wrapper (`latticeGraph`, `D = 2d`) and the cluster-property corollary. |

This lets a future transfer-matrix hyperplane decay estimate feed directly into the `latticeMass` machinery without constructing the transfer-matrix spectral operator. Part of the GJ §17.5 Lemma 17.5.2 sharp transfer-matrix programme (Issue #1645). |

Lemmas: `mem_outerVertexBoundary_iff` (`y ∈ ∂_o^v S ↔ y ∉ S ∧ ∃ x ∈ S, G.Adj x y`), `outerVertexBoundary_disjoint` (`Disjoint (∂_o^v S) S`), `outerVertexBoundary_empty` (`∂_o^v ∅ = ∅`), `outerVertexBoundary_card_le_sum_degrees` (`|∂_o^v S| ≤ ∑ x ∈ S, G.degree x` via `Finset.sdiff_subset` + `Finset.card_biUnion_le` + `card_neighborFinset_eq_degree`). ℤ^d wrapper `IsingModel.Ambient.latticeGraph_outerVertexBoundary_card_le`: `((latticeGraph d).outerVertexBoundary S).card ≤ 2 * d * S.card`, combining the generic sum-of-degrees bound with PR #784's `latticeGraph_degree_le`. Together with PR #784 this exposes the standard outer-vertex-boundary indexing object as preparation for the eventual Simon–Lieb statement (FV Prop 9.31, Epic #780 B-iii). (PR #785.) |
| §5.1 | Inner vertex boundary `∂_i^v S` + outer-by-inner degree bound (Simon–Lieb prep step 3) | **Done (generic def + 3 lemmas + outer-by-inner bound + ℤ^d wrapper)** | `SimpleGraph.innerVertexBoundary G S := S.filter (fun x => ¬ (G.neighborFinset x ⊆ S))` (mathlib's `SimpleGraph` namespace, `Concrete/LatticeGraphBED.lean`) for `[LocallyFinite G] [DecidableEq V]`. Lemmas: `mem_innerVertexBoundary_iff` (`x ∈ ∂_i^v S ↔ x ∈ S ∧ ∃ y, G.Adj x y ∧ y ∉ S` via `Finset.not_subset` + `mem_neighborFinset`), `innerVertexBoundary_subset_self` (`⊆ S` via `Finset.filter_subset`), `innerVertexBoundary_empty` (`∂_i^v ∅ = ∅`). Substantive outer-by-inner boundary degree bound `outerVertexBoundary_card_le_sum_degrees_innerVertexBoundary`: `(∂_o^v S).card ≤ ∑ x ∈ ∂_i^v S, G.degree x` — every outer-boundary vertex `y` is reached as a neighbour of some inner-boundary vertex `x` (the witness for `y ∈ ∂_o^v S` has the outside neighbour `y`, hence sits in `∂_i^v S`); `outerVertexBoundary G S ⊆ (innerVertexBoundary G S).biUnion neighborFinset`, then `Finset.card_biUnion_le` + `card_neighborFinset_eq_degree`. The outer boundary is upper-bounded by a sum of degrees ranging only over the inner boundary. ℤ^d wrapper `latticeGraph_outerVertexBoundary_card_le_two_mul_d_mul_innerVertexBoundary_card`: `((latticeGraph d).∂_o^v S).card ≤ 2d · ((latticeGraph d).∂_i^v S).card` — the elementary max-degree-based linear bound on `ℤ^d` (not the optimal vertex-isoperimetric inequality). (PR #786.) |

ℤ^d wrapper `latticeGraph_edgeBoundary_card_le_two_mul_d_mul_innerVertexBoundary_card`: `((latticeGraph d).∂^e S).card ≤ 2d · ((latticeGraph d).∂_i^v S).card`. | §5.1 | Edge boundary card disjoint biUnion equality (≤ → =) | **Done (PR #787 bound strengthened to equality)** | `SimpleGraph.edgeBoundary_card_eq_sum_inner_filter` (`Concrete/LatticeGraphBED.lean`): `(edgeBoundary G S).card = ∑ x ∈ innerVertexBoundary G S, ((neighborFinset x).filter (· ∉ S)).card`. The `biUnion` defining `edgeBoundary` is disjoint across `x ∈ ∂_i^v S` (different first coordinates), so `Finset.card_biUnion` applies; each summand's image cardinality equals the filter's via `Finset.card_image_of_injective` (`y ↦ (x, y)` injective in `y`). Bounding each filter cardinality by `(neighborFinset x).card = G.degree x` recovers PR #787's inequality `edgeBoundary_card_le_sum_degrees_innerVertexBoundary`. (PR #788.) |

Proof: rewrite `edgeBoundary G S` as a disjoint `biUnion` indexed by `y ∈ ∂_o^v S` via `Finset.ext` (forward / backward use `mem_edgeBoundary_iff`, `mem_outerVertexBoundary_iff`, and `G.symm` to swap adjacency), then `Finset.card_biUnion` (disjointness across distinct second coordinates) + `Finset.card_image_of_injective` (`x ↦ (x, y)` injective in `x`). Symmetric proof for the outer-side bound via `mem_outerVertexBoundary_iff`, `G.symm`, and PR #789's `edgeBoundary_card_eq_sum_outer_filter`. Together with the existing edge-boundary bounds these give the linear chain `|∂_i^v|, |∂_o^v| ≤ |∂^e| ≤ deg_max · |∂_i^v|` (on `latticeGraph d` the rightmost is `2d · |∂_i^v|`, PR #787 + #784). (PR #790.) |

Proof uses the Källén-Lehmann spectral representation S(p) = Z/(p²+m²) + spectral integral, the inverse propagator r(p) = -S(p)⁻¹, and the field strength renormalization constant Z. The old derivative-limit / Cauchy route (closed #2931/#2965; future #3026/#3044/#3054) is retained as future refinement infrastructure and is not required for this non-sharp sandwich. | §17.5 | Lemma 17.5.2 Part B upper bound closed via large-`K` uniform transfer | **Done (unconditional positive-temperature upper bound `m ≤ const·m⁻`, non-sharp constant)** | `exists_pos_forall_pseudoMassG_ge_one_near_zero`, `exists_K_forall_pseudoMassG_ge_one_of_rate_bound`, `exists_uniform_transfer_pseudoMassG_of_rate_bound`, `neg_log_tanh_betaJ_nonneg`, `admissible_rate_le_neg_log_tanh`, `exists_uniform_transfer_pseudoMassG`, and `lemma_17_5_2_upper_bound_uniform_transfer` (`Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/Lemma_17_5_2/UniformTransferLargeK.lean`) discharge the uniform `pseudoMassG` transfer bound `Lemma_17_5_2_UniformTransferPseudoMassGBound`, closing the upper-bound side of GJ Lemma 17.5.2 `m(σ) ≤ const·m⁻(σ)` for ferromagnetic positive-temperature active pairs (`0 < d, J, β`, `1 ≤ α`, `0 < r`). Mechanism: `pseudoMassG α r` is continuous with value `2` at `0` and antitone, so it stays `≥ 1` on a neighbourhood `[0, δ]`; every infinite-volume correlation is uniformly `≤ 1` (`correlationInfinite_le_one`, the uniform gap below `2`) and every admissible decay rate is `≤ -log(tanh(βJ))` (`HasExponentialDecay_rate_le_neg_log_tanh_betaJ`, transferred to an arbitrary exhaustion), so a single `K` (depending only on `α, r, d, J, β`, not on the rate or pair) forces `(a:ℝ)/K ≤ δ`, giving `correlationInfinite ≤ 1 ≤ pseudoMassG α r ((a:ℝ)/K)`. `lemma_17_5_2_upper_bound_uniform_transfer` then yields `∃ K, latticeMass ≤ ofReal K · ofReal m⁻(x,z)`. The constant is uniform but **not sharp**: this proves the qualitative GJ statement (existence of a constant) via the uniform pseudo-mass lower bound `m⁻(x,z) ≥ pseudoMassG⁻¹(1)` that `correlationInfinite ≤ 1` yields, not the sharp transfer-matrix correlation length. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.5 Lemma 17.5.2, pp. 311--312. (Part of #3378, Part of #1645.) |

The `_forall` form exposes a single `K` (depending only on `α, r, d, J, β`) valid for **all** active+profile pairs, matching the book's uniform `m ≤ const·m⁻`. | §17.5 | Lemma 17.5.2 HLS correlation pair-product capstone (Step 119 plan Step 5.6) | **Done (abstract bridge + HLS sum capstone)** | `PseudoMassLatticeDistanceBridge` structure and `tsum_correlationInfinite_pair_product_le_HLS_const` (`IsingModel/PseudoMass/HLSCorrelationCapstone.lean`, new file): abstracts the pseudo-mass-to-lattice-distance lower bound `M_inf · d(x,z) ≤ m⁻·r'` (together with the ferromagnetic assumption and per-pair active-range membership) as a structure, and uses it to derive the GJ p. 312 HLS-form sum bound `∑_z ⟨φ(x₀)φ(z)⟩·⟨φ(y₀)φ(z)⟩ ≤ K` for any `x₀, y₀ : Fin d → ℤ`, where `K = 4 · (max(1, (M_inf^α)⁻¹) · 2^α)² · K_HLS`. Hypotheses: `1 ≤ α`, `0 < r'`, `d < 2 * α`. Proof outline: (i) at `z = x₀` or `z = y₀`, `{x, x} = {x}` (Finset insert idempotent) and the singleton correlation vanishes by the h = 0 Z₂ symmetry on odd cardinality, so the pair product is 0; (ii) for `z ∉ {x₀, y₀}`, Step 5.1 (#3154) gives `corr ≤ 2/(1+(m⁻·r')^α)`, `bridge.bound` gives `m⁻·r' ≥ M_inf·d`, and monotonicity yields `corr ≤ 2/(1+(M_inf·d)^α)`; (iii) the pair-product sum is then bounded via #3170 (`discrete_hls_pseudoMass_two_pair_convolution_constant`). Summability of the LHS is reconstructed from the AM-GM bound `((1+d_x)^(-2α) + (1+d_y)^(-2α))/2`, paralleling `tsum_pseudoMass_pair_product_le_const_pow_M`. The abstract bridge can be supplied by the conditional family constructor when its inputs are already available, but the positive high-temperature route should use the direct Simon-Lieb trichotomy constructors with their adjacent/bound/active inputs. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe §17.5 p. 312. |

| §17.5 / §5.1 | Simon--Lieb one-step decay on the integer lattice (future derivative-route support) | **Done (spatial decay and convergence-rate infrastructure)** | `SimonLiebDistanceDecay.lean` proves `correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_le_of_neighbors_le`: for a non-adjacent pair `i ≠ j` on `ℤ^d`, if every neighbour `k` of `i` satisfies `⟨σ_kσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ C` (`C ≥ 0`), then `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ βJ · 2d · C`, by the Simon--Lieb peeling inequality `correlationInfinite_simon_lieb_latticeGraph` and the degree bound `latticeGraph_degree_le` (degree `≤ 2d`). The second iterate `correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_le_betaJ_two_d_sq_of_dist_ge_three` shows naive peeling *does* iterate once the separation is large enough: for `dist(i,j) ≥ 3` every neighbour `k` of `i` still satisfies `dist(k,j) ≥ dist(i,j) − 1 ≥ 2`, hence is non-adjacent to `j` and obeys `⟨σ_kσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ βJ·2d`, so `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ (βJ·2d)²` (squaring the contraction factor). Iterating fully, `correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_le_betaJ_two_d_pow_of_dist_gt` gives `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ (βJ·2d)^n` whenever `dist(i,j) ≥ n + 1`, i.e. `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ (βJ·2d)^{dist(i,j) − 1}` — prefactor-free geometric decay with explicit base `βJ·2d` (no contraction-factor abstraction and no ball-boundary shell axiom), by induction on `n` (the `n = 0` base bounds by `1`; each step peels via `_le_of_neighbors_le` with `C = (βJ·2d)^n`). The same reverse-triangle step continues while the separation from `j` stays `≥ 2`; the obstruction is the distance-`2` base case (a neighbour can be *adjacent* to `j`, bounded only by `1`, with no `≤ βJ·2d` bound for adjacent pairs), which caps the gain near `j`. A clean prefactor-free exponential distance decay (one contraction per shell, with no such near-`j` defect) instead uses the separating-surface (ball-boundary) Simon--Lieb argument `ball_boundary_simon_lieb` applied to cubic shells. That spatial decay is in fact already available via the shell iteration `shellSup_iterated_bound` (`TheoremEtaLe1/Contraction.lean`); its pointwise form `correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_le_contractionFactor_pow_dist` gives `⟨σ_0σ_y⟩^∞ ≤ (contractionFactor d Λ p r)^{dist(0,y)/(r+2)}` for every `y ≠ 0` (prefactor-free, contractionFactor `< 1`), and the translation-invariant form `correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_le_contractionFactor_pow_dist_pair` extends it to every distinct pair `⟨σ_iσ_j⟩^∞ ≤ (contractionFactor)^{dist(i,j)/(r+2)}`. The summability form `correlationInfinite_latticeGraph_susceptibility_summable` records that, when `0 < contractionFactor < 1`, the correlation kernel is summable over `ℤ^d` (finite magnetic susceptibility `χ = ∑_y ⟨σ_0σ_y⟩^∞`): the per-pair decay is dominated by `(1/contractionFactor)·exp(-m·dist)` with `m = -log(contractionFactor)/(r+2) > 0`, summable by `summable_exp_neg_dist`. (Steps 503-548, 576-615; PRs #1517-#1566; Issue #1344.) **Mayer Phase B `D_n` foundation** (`ClusterExpansion/AlternatingCompleteGraph.lean`, Part of #1499): toward the general-`n` Mayer coefficient identity `alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum K_n = (-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!` (base cases `n ≤ 4` already done) via the root-component recurrence `D_n = ∑_{C ∋ 0} c_{|C|} D_{n-|C|}` (`c = alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum`, `D = allSignedSubgraphSum` the signed sum over *all* spanning edge-subsets). `allSignedSubgraphSum_eq_zero_of_edgeFinset_nonempty` (`D = 0` when there is an edge, via `Finset.sum_powerset_neg_one_pow_card_of_nonempty`), `_eq_one_of_edgeFinset_empty` (`D = 1` edgeless), `allSignedSubgraphSum_completeGraph_eq_zero_of_two_le` (`D_n = 0`, `n ≥ 2`) and `_eq_one_of_subsingleton` (`D_n = 1`, `n ≤ 1`) establish the `D_n` boundary values for the recurrence. **Iso-invariance** `allSignedSubgraphSum_iso` and `alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum_iso` (for `φ : G ≃g H`, `D`/`c` are graph-isomorphism invariants): the edge-relabelling `S ↦ S.map (Sym2.map φ)` is a cardinality-preserving (and, for `c`, connectivity-preserving via `SimpleGraph.Iso.connected_iff`) bijection on edge-subsets. Supplies the `c_{|C|} = c(K_{|C|})`, `D_{n-|C|} = D(K_{n-|C|})` ingredients of the recurrence via `K_n|_C ≅ K_{|C|}`. **Bijection foundations**: `alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum_completeGraph_card` / `allSignedSubgraphSum_completeGraph_card` (`c`/`D` of `K_V` depend only on `|V|`, iso-invariance applied to `K_V ≅ K_{Fin |V|}`); `connectedComponentMk_eq_of_mem` (edges of `S` do not cross components of `fromEdgeSet ↑S`, via `connectedComponentMk_eq_of_adj` — the crossing-edge-free property underlying the root-component split). **Root-component vertex set** (`ClusterExpansion/MayerRootComponent.lean`): `rootComponentFinset S r` = vertices in the connected component of `r` in `fromEdgeSet ↑S`; `mem_rootComponentFinset`, `self_mem_rootComponentFinset` (`r ∈` its own component), and `mem_rootComponentFinset_iff_of_mem_edge` (for `s(a,b) ∈ S`, `a ∈ C ↔ b ∈ C` — both endpoints fall in the root component together), the set-level crossing-edge-free property for the `D_n = ∑_{C ∋ 0} c_{|C|} D_{n-|C|}` split. **Edge-count split** `rootComponent_edge_card_split` (`#(S∩C.sym2) + #(S∩Cᶜ.sym2) = #S` via `Finset.sym2` + `Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not` + crossing-free). **Inside-connected crux** `induce_fromEdgeSet_inside_connected` (the within-`C` edges `S ∩ C.sym2` induce a *connected* graph on `C`): since `↑C = (fromEdgeSet ↑S).connectedComponentMk r).supp` (`coe_rootComponentFinset`) and the inside edges induce the same graph on `C` as `S` (`induce_fromEdgeSet_inside_eq`), the induced graph is the component's `toSimpleGraph`, connected by `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.connected_toSimpleGraph`. The hardest ingredient of the multiplicative split — that `S_in` is connected-spanning on `C`. **Root-component fibre product split** (`MayerRootComponent.lean`): `reachable_stays_in_of_no_cross` (with no crossing edge, reachability from the root stays inside `C`, via `Relation.ReflTransGen` induction on the reachability witness); `rootComponentFinset_eq_iff` (the fibre characterisation `rootComponentFinset S r = C ↔ r ∈ C ∧ (no edge of S crosses C) ∧ (S ∩ C.sym2 induces a connected graph on C)`, packaging `induce_fromEdgeSet_inside_connected` forwards and `reachable_stays_in_of_no_cross` backwards); `mem_sym2_and_compl_sym2_false` (`C.sym2` and `Cᶜ.sym2` are disjoint); the inside/outside ambient signed-subgraph sets `insideConnectedEdgeSubsets`, `outsideEdgeSubsets` with their membership lemmas; and the **lemma-6 capstone** `fiber_signed_sum_eq_product`: `∑_{S : rootComponentFinset S r = C} (-1)^|S| = (∑_{A ∈ inside} (-1)^|A|) · (∑_{B ∈ outside} (-1)^|B|)`, proved by the crossing-free bijection `S ↦ (S ∩ C.sym2, S ∩ Cᶜ.sym2)` with inverse `(A, B) ↦ A ∪ B` (`Finset.sum_bij'`), with `rootComponent_edge_card_split` giving `|S| = |A| + |B|` so `(-1)^|S| = (-1)^|A|·(-1)^|B|`. The ambient multiplicative core of the recurrence `D_n = ∑_{C ∋ 0} c_{|C|} D_{n-|C|}` (GJ §18.4). Still **Partial**: the fibrewise summation over `C` with the reindex `inside ≅ c(K_C)`, `outside ≅ D(K_{Cᶜ})` collapsing to the closed form `(-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!` is done (the general `K_n` formula below); the remaining gap is the general-`t` Mayer expansion identity (Issue #1499). **Fibrewise recurrence + outside factor** (`MayerRootComponent.lean`): `real_signed_sum_powerset` (`∑_{B ⊆ X} (-1)^|B| = if X = ∅ then 1 else 0`, real-cast of `Finset.sum_powerset_neg_one_pow_card`); `allSignedSubgraphSum_eq_ite` (`D(G) = if G.edgeFinset = ∅ then 1 else 0`); the **lemma-7 fibrewise sum** `allSignedSubgraphSum_eq_sum_fiber_product`: `D(G) = ∑_{C : r ∈ C} insideΣ(C)·outsideΣ(C)` via `Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to` on the root-component map `S ↦ rootComponentFinset S r` together with the per-fibre product split; and the outside-factor evaluation `outsideEdgeSubsets_eq_powerset` (the outside subsets are exactly the powerset of `G.edgeFinset ∩ Cᶜ.sym2`) + `outsideEdgeSubsets_signed_sum_eq_ite` (`outsideΣ(C) = if G.edgeFinset ∩ Cᶜ.sym2 = ∅ then 1 else 0`). The Kotecký–Preiss tree-sum induction builds on this. **Ursell tree bound** (`ClusterExpansion/UrsellTreeBound.lean`, entry of milestone M2): lifting the Penrose inequality to the Ursell coefficient, `ursellCoefficient_abs_le_numSpanningTrees_div_factorial` (`|ϕ^T(ω)| ≤ numSpanningTrees (polymerSeqIncompatibilityGraph ω) / n!`) and the uniform form `ursellCoefficient_abs_le_numSpanningTrees_top_div_factorial` (`≤ numSpanningTrees (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) / n!`, via `Penrose.numSpanningTrees_mono` + `le_top`) — the sharp replacement of the trivial `2^|E|/n!` bound, feeding the convergence majorant. **Complete-graph spanning-tree count bound** (`Penrose/CompleteGraphTreeBound.lean`, milestone M2): `numSpanningTrees_top_fin_le_pow_pred` (`numSpanningTrees (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) ≤ n^(n-1)`, unconditional) with its `Fin (n+1)` form `numSpanningTrees_top_fin_succ_le_pow` (`≤ (n+1)^n`), proved by a **parent-function injection** avoiding Prüfer/Cayley: `treeParent` (the unique neighbour of a non-root vertex decreasing its distance to the root by one, packaged by `existsUnique_parent_adj_dist_of_isTree` = `exists_parent_adj_dist_of_isTree` + `parent_adj_dist_unique_of_isTree`, using `IsTree.existsUnique_path` and the shortest-walk second vertex), the parent code `completeGraphTreeParentCode : Fin n → Fin (n+1)`, the **edge-set recovery** `completeGraphTree_edges_eq_parentCode_image` (the edge set of a spanning tree of `K_{n+1}` is exactly the image of its parent code — each tree edge is the parent edge of its endpoint farther from the root, by `IsTree.dist_eq_dist_add_one_of_adj`), hence `completeGraphTreeParentCode_injective` and the count bound via `Fintype.card_le_of_injective` + `Fintype.card_fun`. The weaker `n^(n-1)` (not Cayley's exact `n^(n-2)`) already yields the Mayer-series radius `1/e`, since `∑ₙ n^(n-1)/n!·Rⁿ` converges absolutely for `|R| < 1/e` (ratio `(1+1/n)^(n-1)·|R| → e·|R|`); the remaining M2 steps reconstruct the summable Mayer majorant from the Ursell tree bound and the Kotecký–Preiss `log Ξ = ∑` cluster identity. **Summable Mayer majorant** (`Penrose/SpanningTreeSummable.lean`, milestone M2): the real-analysis core `summable_completeGraph_numSpanningTrees_div_factorial_mul_pow` (`Summable (fun n => numSpanningTrees (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) / n! · Rⁿ)` for `e·|R| < 1`, the explicit radius `1/e`) and its absolute form `_abs_pow`, obtained from the pure-power summability `summable_nat_pow_pred_div_factorial_mul_pow` (`Summable (fun n => n^(n-1)/n! · Rⁿ)`) by majorising `numSpanningTrees (⊤ Fin n) ≤ n^(n-1)`. The power series is summable by the **ratio test** (`summable_of_ratio_norm_eventually_le`): the eventual ratio is `(1+1/n)^(n-1)·|R| ≤ e·|R| < 1`, where the elementary bound `one_add_inv_natCast_pow_pred_le_exp` (`(1+1/n)^(n-1) ≤ e`, from `1+x ≤ eˣ` raised to the `(n-1)`-th power, no `(1+1/n)ⁿ → e` limit needed) feeds the post-cancellation inequality `succ_pow_pred_le_exp_mul_pow_pred` (`(n+1)^(n-1) ≤ e·n^(n-1)`). This supplies the convergent majorant for the Mayer/Ursell series; the remaining M2 steps are the Mayer-term reduction `Summable (mayerExpansionTerm G ·)` (Kotecký–Preiss) and `log Ξ = ∑` cluster. **Mayer expansion absolute convergence** (`MayerCore/UrsellMajorant.lean`, milestone M2 capstone): `summable_mayerExpansionTerm_of_exp_one_mul_activity_lt_one` (`Summable (fun n => mayerExpansionTerm G n t)` whenever `e·(∑_{P ∈ allPolymers G} |t|^{|P|}) < 1`) and the usable form `summable_mayerExpansionTerm_of_card_mul_lt` (sufficient: `|t| ≤ 1` and `e·|allPolymers G|·|t| < 1`). The chain: the Ursell coefficient is bounded uniformly `|ϕ^T(ω)| ≤ numSpanningTrees (⊤ Fin n)/n!` (`ursellCoefficient_abs_le_numSpanningTrees_top_div_factorial`, #3993); the total activity over `n`-tuples factorises `∑_{ω} |z(t,ω)| = (∑_{P} |t|^{|P|})^n` (`sum_clusterSeqActivity_abs_piFinset` via `Finset.sum_prod_piFinset`); so `|mayerExpansionTerm G n t| ≤ numSpanningTrees (⊤ Fin n)/n! · A^n` (`mayerExpansionTerm_abs_le_tree_activity_pow`) with `A = ∑_P |t|^{|P|}`, which is exactly the `SpanningTreeSummable` majorant at `R = A`. This is the absolute convergence `∑ₙ mayerExpansionTerm` of the cluster expansion for general interacting polymers; the remaining M2 steps are `log Ξ = ∑ₙ mayerExpansionTerm` (Kotecký–Preiss) and the high-temperature Ising specialisation `t = tanh(βJ)`. **High-temperature Ising convergence** (`MayerCore/MayerTanhConvergence.lean`, milestone M2): specialising to the Ising activity `t = tanh(β·J)`, `summable_mayerExpansionTerm_tanh` (`Summable (fun n => mayerExpansionTerm G n (tanh(β·J)))` for `e·|allPolymers G|·|tanh(β·J)| < 1`) with the ferromagnetic form `summable_mayerExpansionTerm_tanh_ferro` (`0 ≤ β·J`, `e·|allPolymers G|·tanh(β·J) < 1`) and the activity-sum form `_of_activity`; the ferromagnetic activity bound `tanh_activity_sum_le_card_mul_tanh` (`∑_P tanh(β·J)^{|P|} ≤ |allPolymers G|·tanh(β·J)`). Since `tanh` is continuous with `tanh 0 = 0`, the criterion holds at high temperature (`β·J` near `0`) — the Ising cluster expansion **converges absolutely at high temperature**. The remaining step is the Mayer–Montroll identity `log Ξ = ∑ₙ mayerExpansionTerm` (Issue #1499 Phase C). **Mayer–Montroll Phase C — colouring identity + `r!` fibre count** (`MayerCore/SurjectiveLogWeight.lean`, `MayerCore/MayerMontroll.lean`, Issue #1499, **Partial — tsum assembly remains**): the combinatorial core of the general-`t` Mayer identity, via a contraction-free edge inclusion–exclusion. **Surjective log-weight identity** (`SurjectiveLogWeight.lean`, graph-independent): `surjCount n k := #{surjections Fin n → Fin k}` with the surjection recurrence `surjCount_succ_succ` (`surjCount (n+1)(k+1) = (k+1)·(surjCount n (k+1) + surjCount n k)`, via two `Fin`/`Equiv` bijections); the telescoping identity `surjLogWeight_eq` (`∑_{k=1}^n (-1)^(k-1)/k · surjCount n k = [n = 1]`); and the general finite-type form `surjective_logWeight_eq_connected_indicator`. **Mayer–Montroll colouring identity** (`MayerMontroll.lean`, **done**): `mayerMontroll_coloring_identity` — `∑_{k=1}^r (-1)^(k-1)/k · #properSurjectiveColorings H k = alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum H` for any finite graph `H` on `Fin r`, via `badColorEdges`/`proper_indicator_eq_signed_bad_edges` (Boolean inclusion–exclusion over edges), `constantOnEdgeSet_iff_constant_on_components` + `colorings_constant_on_components_equiv` (the inner colour count factors through connected components), the edge expansion `properSurjectiveColorings_card_eq_sum_edges`, `surjLogWeight_sum_Icc_of_le`, and `connected_iff_card_connectedComponent_eq_one`. Bridged to the Ursell coefficient by `ursellCoefficient_eq_coloring_sum` (`ϕ^T(ω) = (∑_k (-1)^(k-1)/k · #properSurjectiveColorings (G(ω)) k)/n!`) and `mayerExpansionTerm_eq_coloring_form`. **`r!` colour-class fibre count** (`MayerMontroll.lean`, **done**): `card_proper_colorClass_fiber` — the `(ω, c)` (polymer sequence + proper colouring) with colour classes equal to a fixed family-tuple `Ω` number exactly `r!` (`r = ∑_a |Ω a|`), via the explicit `Equiv {(ω,c): proper, colorClass = Ω} ≃ (Fin r ≃ ↥labelledPolymers Ω)` (`seqColoringForward` bijection + `invColorClass`/`invProper`) and `Fintype.card_equiv`; the supporting `clusterSeqActivity_eq_prod_colorClass` (each fibre element has activity `∏_a ∏_{P∈Ω a} t^|P|`) and `fiber_sum_clusterSeqActivity` (`∑_{fibre} clusterSeqActivity = r!·W(Ω)`). **Per-`m` family-tuple identity** (`MayerMontroll.lean`, **done**): `vdFamilyTuple_sum_eq_seq_coloring_sum` regroups the family-tuple Mayer sum fibrewise over the colour-class map (`card_proper_colorClass_fiber` supplies the `r!` factor). **Capstone** (`MayerMontroll.lean`, **done**): `mayer_identity_general_t : polymerFreeEnergy G t = ∑'_n mayerExpansionTerm G n t` under the convergence hypotheses `|ε(t)| < 1` (log(1+ε) series) and `e·A < 1` (`A = ∑_P |t|^|P|`, double-sum Fubini), plus the unconditional eventual form `mayer_identity_general_t_eventually` (`∀ᶠ t in nhds 0`). The proof recasts both sides as the colour-degree double sum `colorDegreeTerm G t r k = (-1)^(k-1)/k · ∑_ω #properSurjectiveColorings(G(ω),k)/r! · clusterSeqActivity` (`mayerExpansionTerm_eq_tsum_colorDegreeTerm` row, `logTaylorTerm_eq_tsum_colorDegreeTerm` column), proves double-summability `summable_uncurry_colorDegreeTerm` (row majorant `∑_k|C(r,k)| ≤ (r^r/r!)·A^r` via `tsum_abs_colorDegreeTerm_le` + ratio test `summable_pow_self_div_factorial_mul_abs_pow`), and swaps the order with `Summable.tsum_comm` after shifting away the vanishing `k=0` column (`colorDegreeTerm_eq_zero_of_card_lt`). This completes GJ §18.4 (Mayer–Montroll / cluster identity `log Ξ = ∑ cluster terms`) in the convergence regime. |
| §18.5 | **Interacting Ising free energy as a Mayer expansion** (Issue #3511) | **Done (interacting finite-volume free energy = convergent cluster expansion)** | `ClusterExpansion/MayerCore/InteractingFreeEnergyMayer.lean`. The interacting analogue of the non-interacting `freeEnergy_eq_tsum_mayer_of_pairwise_disjoint`: combining the polymer decomposition `freeEnergy_eq_polymerFreeEnergy` with the general Mayer–Montroll identity `mayer_identity_general_t`, `freeEnergy_eq_tsum_mayer_of_activity` gives, under the convergence hypotheses `|ε(tanh βJ)| < 1` and `e·∑_P |tanh βJ|^|P| < 1` (and `0 ≤ βJ`, `0 < |ι|`), `freeEnergy G ⟨J,0,β⟩ = log 2 + (|E|/|ι|)·log cosh(βJ) + (∑'_n mayerExpansionTerm G n (tanh βJ))/|ι|`. A ferromagnetic-hypothesis form `freeEnergy_eq_tsum_mayer_of_activity_ferromagnetic` (`0 ≤ J`, `0 < β`) is included. This removes the pairwise-vertex-disjoint restriction of the non-interacting case, expressing the interacting finite-volume free energy directly through its convergent cluster terms — the finite-volume step toward the §18.5 infinite-volume analyticity of the pressure (the convergence hypotheses' high-temperature discharge and the volume-uniform / infinite-volume limit are later work). Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 378–386 (cluster-expansion convergence of the pressure / free energy). |
| §18.5 | **High-temperature discharge of the interacting Mayer expansion** (Issue #3511) | **Done (interacting free energy = Mayer expansion under explicit high-temperature conditions)** | `ClusterExpansion/MayerCore/InteractingFreeEnergyMayerHighTemp.lean`. Discharges the two convergence hypotheses of `freeEnergy_eq_tsum_mayer_of_activity` from explicit finite-graph high-temperature smallness: `mayer_log_condition_of_one_add_pow_lt_two` (`|ε(t)|<1` from `(1+t)^|E|<2`, via `0≤ε≤(1+t)^|E|−1`) and `mayer_activity_condition_tanh_of_card_mul_lt` (`e·∑_P|tanh βJ|^|P|<1` from `e·|allPolymers G|·tanh(βJ)<1`, via `∑_P tanh^|P| ≤ |allPolymers G|·tanh`). The headline `freeEnergy_eq_tsum_mayer_of_high_temp` (+ `_ferromagnetic`) gives `freeEnergy G ⟨J,0,β⟩ = log 2 + (|E|/|ι|)·log cosh(βJ) + (∑'_n mayerExpansionTerm)/|ι|` under `(1+tanh βJ)^|E|<2 ∧ e·|allPolymers G|·tanh(βJ)<1` (both trivially satisfied as βJ→0), with no separate convergence hypotheses. Finite-volume; the volume-uniform / infinite-volume analyticity of the pressure is later work. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 378–386. |
| §18.5 | **Λ-layer / along-exhaustion high-temperature Mayer expansion** (Issue #3511) | **Done (per-volume Λ and along-exhaustion wrappers)** | `AmbientLattice/SpecialCases/InteractingFreeEnergyMayerHighTemp.lean`. Λ-layer and along-exhaustion wrappers of `freeEnergy_eq_tsum_mayer_of_high_temp`: `freeEnergyΛ_eq_tsum_mayer_of_high_temp` (+ `_ferromagnetic`) and `freeEnergyAlongExhaustion_eq_tsum_mayer_of_high_temp` (+ `_ferromagnetic`) give, on a nonempty finite volume `Λ` (resp. each exhaustion stage `n`) satisfying the explicit high-temperature conditions on the induced graph, `freeEnergyΛ G Λ ⟨J,0,β⟩ = log 2 + (|E_Λ|/|Λ|)·log cosh(βJ) + (∑'_n mayerExpansionTerm (inducedGraph G Λ) n (tanh βJ))/|Λ|` (composing the core theorem at `inducedGraph G Λ` via `Finset.Nonempty.fintype_card_coe_pos`). These are **per-volume** statements: the high-temperature conditions `(1+tanh βJ)^|E_Λ|<2` and `e·|allPolymers(inducedGraph G Λ)|·tanh(βJ)<1` grow with `|Λ|`, so for fixed positive `tanh(βJ)` they fail at large volume — a volume-uniform Kotecky–Preiss / Dobrushin activity bound (not these per-volume conditions) is what a genuine infinite-volume Mayer pressure identity requires (later work). Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 378–386. |
| §18.5 | **Rooted polymer counting (volume-uniform max-degree bound)** (Issue #3511) | **Done (FV (3.49) rooted polymer count ≤ Δ^{2ℓ})** | `ClusterExpansion/PolymerCounting.lean`. The volume-uniform combinatorial input to the Kotecky–Preiss criterion: `rootedPolymers G v` (polymers whose support contains `v`), `rootedPolymersOfCard G v ℓ` (those of size `ℓ`), `rootedPolymersOfCard_card_le_closedWalkCount` (`(rootedPolymersOfCard G v ℓ).card ≤ (G.finsetWalkLength (2ℓ) v v).card`, via the FV §3.7.3 injection `card_connected_edge_sets_le` — polymers are connected edge sets, mapped to closed walks of length `2ℓ`), and the headline `rootedPolymersOfCard_card_le_maxDegree_pow` (`(rootedPolymersOfCard G v ℓ).card ≤ G.maxDegree^{2ℓ}`, chaining the walk injection with `walksFromCount_le_pow` via `degree_le_maxDegree`). This count depends only on the max degree, NOT on the volume — the first reusable volume-uniform object for the §18.5 infinite-volume cluster expansion (unlike the per-volume conditions of the high-temperature wrappers). The per-vertex activity geometric bound `∑_{P∋v} t^|P| ≤ (1−Δ²t)⁻¹` and the volume-uniform Mayer convergence are the next assembly. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 378–386; Friedli–Velenik §3.7.3 eq. (3.49). |
| §18.5 | **Per-vertex polymer activity bound (volume-uniform)** (Issue #3954) | **Done (geometric series `∑_{P∋v} t^|P| ≤ (1−Δ²t)⁻¹`)** | `ClusterExpansion/PolymerActivity.lean`. Sums the volume-uniform rooted polymer count of `PolymerCounting` against the activity weight. `rootedPolymerActivity G v t := ∑_{P ∈ rootedPolymers G v} t^|P|` and the headline `rootedPolymerActivity_le_geometric` (`0 ≤ t`, `Δ²t < 1 ⟹ rootedPolymerActivity G v t ≤ (1 − Δ²t)⁻¹`, `Δ = G.maxDegree`): partition `rootedPolymers G v` by cardinality (`Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to`), bound each size-`ℓ` fibre by `(rootedPolymersOfCard G v ℓ).card · t^ℓ ≤ Δ^{2ℓ}·t^ℓ = (Δ²t)^ℓ` via `rootedPolymersOfCard_card_le_maxDegree_pow`, then dominate the finite sum by the infinite geometric series `∑'_ℓ (Δ²t)^ℓ = (1−Δ²t)⁻¹` (`Summable.sum_le_tsum`, `tsum_geometric_of_lt_one`). The bound depends only on the maximum degree, not on the volume — the per-vertex Kotecky–Preiss activity input that survives the infinite-volume limit, unlike the per-volume conditions of `InteractingFreeEnergyMayerHighTemp`. Assembling the full volume-uniform Kotecky–Preiss convergence from it is later work. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 378–386; Friedli–Velenik §3.7.3 eq. (3.49). |
| §18.5 | **Total / per-site polymer activity bound (volume-uniform)** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`∑_P t^|P| ≤ |ι|·(1−Δ²t)⁻¹`; per-site `≤ (1−Δ²t)⁻¹`)** | `ClusterExpansion/PolymerActivity.lean`. Double-counts the per-vertex activity bound over all vertices. `allPolymersActivity G t := ∑_{P ∈ allPolymers G} t^|P|`; helper `one_le_card_polymerSupport_of_mem_allPolymers` (a polymer touches ≥ 1 vertex, via `Sym2.ind`/`Sym2.mem_mk_left`); `sum_rootedPolymerActivity_eq` (`∑_v ∑_{P∋v} t^|P| = ∑_P |supp P|·t^|P|`, by `Finset.sum_comm` + `Finset.sum_ite_mem`/`univ_inter`). Headline `allPolymersActivity_le_card_mul_geometric` (`0 ≤ t`, `Δ²t < 1 ⟹ ∑_P t^|P| ≤ |ι|·(1−Δ²t)⁻¹`): each polymer is counted at least once in the vertex sum (`1 ≤ |supp P|`), so the total activity is dominated by `∑_v rootedPolymerActivity G v t ≤ |ι|` copies of the per-vertex geometric bound. Corollary `allPolymersActivity_div_card_le_geometric` (`Nonempty ι`): the **per-site** activity `(1/|ι|)·∑_P t^|P| ≤ (1−Δ²t)⁻¹` — bounded by a volume-uniform constant depending only on `Δ = G.maxDegree`. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 378–386; Friedli–Velenik §3.7.3 eq. (3.49). |
| §18.5 | **Weighted per-vertex + incompatibility-neighbourhood activity bounds (Kotecký–Preiss inputs)** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`∑_{Q∼P}(e\|t\|)^\|Q\| ≤ \|supp P\|·(1−Δ²e\|t\|)⁻¹`)** | `ClusterExpansion/PolymerActivityKP.lean`. The local (per-vertex), `e`-weighted activity inputs to the Kotecký–Preiss criterion, built on `rootedPolymerActivity_le_geometric`. `rootedPolymerActivity_expWeighted_le_geometric` (`Δ²·e\|t\| < 1 ⟹ ∑_{Q∋v} e^\|Q\|·\|t\|^\|Q\| ≤ (1−Δ²e\|t\|)⁻¹`, the substitution `t ↦ e\|t\|`). `incompatiblePolymers G P := (allPolymers G).filter (PolymersIncompatible P)`; headline `incompatibilityActivity_expWeighted_le` (`∑_{Q∼P} (e\|t\|)^\|Q\| ≤ \|supp P\|·(1−Δ²e\|t\|)⁻¹`): each polymer incompatible with `P` shares a support vertex (`PolymersIncompatible.iff_exists_shared_vertex`), so the neighbourhood activity is bounded by `\|supp P\|` copies of the per-vertex geometric bound (witness-count `≥ 1` + `Finset.sum_comm` + subset of `rootedPolymers G v`). This `∑_{Q∼P}(e\|t\|)^\|Q\| ≤ \|supp P\|·(...)⁻¹` estimate is the direct input to the KP / rooted-cluster tree induction; both bounds are volume-uniform (max-degree only). Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4, KP criterion), §5.7.1 (Ising application). |
| §18.5 | **Kotecký–Preiss hypothesis discharged at high temperature (FV Thm 5.4)** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`∑_{Q∼P} e^\|Q\|·\|t\|^\|Q\| ≤ \|P\|` for `Δ²e\|t\| ≤ ½`)** | `ClusterExpansion/PolymerActivityKP.lean`. Sharpens the activity bound to the *tail* geometric series and discharges the FV Theorem 5.4 KP hypothesis with weight `a(P) = \|P\|`. `rootedPolymerActivity_le_geometric_tail` (polymers are nonempty so the activity sum starts at edge-count 1: `∑_{Q∋v} u^\|Q\| ≤ (Δ²u)·(1−Δ²u)⁻¹`, the tail that vanishes as `u→0` — proved by the `ℓ=0` fibre being empty + `Summable.tsum_eq_zero_add`). `polymerSupport_card_le_card_of_mem_allPolymers` (`\|supp P\| ≤ \|P\|` via the handshake `sum_filter_card_eq_two_mul_card`: every support vertex of an even subgraph has even degree `≥ 2`, so `2\|supp P\| ≤ ∑_v deg = 2\|P\|`). Headline `incompatibilityActivity_expWeighted_le_card_of_half` (`Δ²e\|t\| ≤ ½ ⟹ ∑_{Q∼P} e^\|Q\|·\|t\|^\|Q\| ≤ \|P\|`): the tail per-vertex bound `Δ²e\|t\|·(1−Δ²e\|t\|)⁻¹ ≤ 1` (valid for `Δ²e\|t\| ≤ ½`) summed over the `≤ \|P\|` support vertices. This is the exact volume-uniform input that a Kotecký–Preiss cluster-expansion convergence theorem consumes. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |

Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |
| §18.5 | **Weighted spanning-tree sum dominated by a product of per-vertex sums** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`∑_T ∏_i c i (parentCode T i) ≤ ∏_i ∑_p c i p`)** | `ClusterExpansion/Penrose/WeightedTreeSum.lean`. The combinatorial heart of the KP tree-graph bound — a *weighted* version of the parent-code count bound `numSpanningTrees (⊤ Fin (n+1)) ≤ (n+1)^n` (= `numSpanningTrees (⊤ Fin n) ≤ n^(n-1)`; the parent-function relaxation, weaker than Cayley's exact `(n+1)^(n-1)`), reusing the existing parent-code injection `completeGraphTreeParentCode_injective`. `completeGraphTreeParentCode_sum_le_sum_all_parentCodes` (`∑_{T spanning tree} F (parentCode T) ≤ ∑_{p : Fin n → Fin (n+1)} F p` for `0 ≤ F`, via `Finset.sum_image` + `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg`: spanning trees inject into parent functions, so the tree sum is a sub-sum of the full parent-function sum). `completeGraphTreeParentCode_weighted_sum_le_prod_parentSums` (product weight `F p = ∏_i c i (p i)`: `∑_T ∏_i c i (parentCode T i) ≤ ∏_i ∑_p c i p`, factorising the unconstrained parent sum over independent vertex choices via `Fintype.prod_sum`). Converts a sum over the *constrained* spanning trees into a product of *independent* per-vertex sums — the latter being the per-vertex Kotecký–Preiss activity sums. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4, tree-graph inequality). |
| §18.5 | **Monotonicity of spanning-tree edge subsets** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`spanningTreeEdgeSubsets G ⊆ spanningTreeEdgeSubsets H` for `G ≤ H`)** | `ClusterExpansion/Penrose/SpanningTreeMono.lean`. A spanning tree of a subgraph `G ≤ H` is a spanning tree of `H` (same vertices, edges in `G.edgeFinset ⊆ H.edgeFinset`, connectivity + edge-count unchanged): `spanningTreeEdgeSubsets_mono` (via `mem_spanningTreeEdgeSubsets` + `SimpleGraph.edgeFinset_subset_edgeFinset`), the weighted consequence `sum_spanningTree_le_of_le` (`0 ≤ F ⟹ ∑_{S ∈ spanningTreeEdgeSubsets G} F S ≤ ∑_{S ∈ spanningTreeEdgeSubsets H} F S`), and the `⊤` specialization `sum_spanningTree_le_top`. This lets a weighted sum over the spanning trees of any graph (e.g. a polymer incompatibility graph) be dominated by the same sum over the spanning trees of `⊤`, where the parent-code factorisation of `WeightedTreeSum` applies. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |

Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4, tree-graph inequality). |

| §18.5 | **A complete-graph spanning tree has a non-root leaf** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`∃ j, ∀ i, parentCode T i ≠ succ j`)** | `ClusterExpansion/Penrose/CompleteTreeLeaf.lean`. The rooted-tree KP induction peels leaves (vertices that are nobody's parent). `completeGraphTreeParentCode_exists_nonroot_leaf` (`n > 0`): the vertex `v` farthest from the root `0` (`Finset.exists_max_image` of `H.dist 0`) is a non-root leaf — `v ≠ 0` (else all vertices have distance `0`, so equal `0` by `Connected.dist_eq_zero_iff`, contradicting `n > 0`), and if `v = succ j` were the parent of some `succ i` then `treeParent_spec` gives `dist 0 (succ i) = dist 0 v + 1 > dist 0 v`, contradicting maximality. | §18.5 | **Polynomial-moment bound for the geometric series** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`∑_ℓ ℓ^d r^ℓ ≤ d!/(1−r)^{d+1}`)** | `ClusterExpansion/GeometricMoment.lean`. The analytic ingredient for the tree-route Kotecký–Preiss leaf-peel induction (summing a leaf into its parent leaves a `\|parent\|`-power factor; iterating accumulates polynomial moments of the per-vertex activity). `tsum_pow_mul_geometric_le` (`0 ≤ r < 1`): `∑'_ℓ ℓ^d r^ℓ ≤ d!·(1−r)^{−(d+1)}`. Each `ℓ^d` is dominated termwise by `d!·\binom{ℓ+d}{d}` (`ℓ^d ≤ (ℓ+1)^d ≤ (ℓ+d)^{\underline d} = d!·\binom{ℓ+d}{d}` via `Nat.pow_sub_le_descFactorial` + `Nat.descFactorial_eq_factorial_mul_choose`), and the negative-binomial geometric series sums to `(1−r)^{−(d+1)}` (`tsum_choose_mul_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`); termwise comparison by `Summable.tsum_le_tsum` with `summable_pow_mul_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |

| §18.5 | **Rooted-parent active-set scaffolding (leaf-peel induction)** (Issue #3954) | **Done (active-vertex / closed / leaf predicates + erase-leaf lemmas)** | `ClusterExpansion/RootedParentActive.lean`. The combinatorial scaffolding for the rooted-tree KP leaf-peel induction, which recurses by removing a leaf of an active vertex set rather than re-deriving a shrinking tree's parent code. `rootedParentActiveVertices A := insert 0 (A.image Fin.succ)` (root `0` + active non-root vertices), `succ_mem_rootedParentActiveVertices`, `RootedParentActiveClosed par A` (every active vertex's parent is active/root), `RootedParentLeaf par A j` (`j ∈ A` is nobody's parent in `A`). The two induction-step facts: `RootedParentActiveClosed.erase_leaf` (erasing a leaf preserves active-closedness — an active `i ≠ j` cannot have parent `Fin.succ j` since `j` is a leaf) and `RootedParentLeaf.parent_mem_erase` (the leaf's parent stays active after the erase). Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |
| §18.5 | **Leaf existence for the rooted-parent active-set induction** (Issue #3954) | **Done (rank-decreasing parent ⟹ leaf in every nonempty active set)** | `ClusterExpansion/RootedParentLeafExistence.lean`. The leaf-peel induction needs that a nonempty active set has a leaf. `exists_rootedParentLeaf_of_rank` (abstract: if `rank (par i) < rank (Fin.succ i)` for all `i`, then the maximal-rank active vertex is a leaf — any vertex it parented would have strictly larger rank, `Finset.exists_max_image` + `omega`). `completeGraphTreeParentCode_rank_lt` (the parent code strictly decreases the tree distance from the root, via `treeParent_spec`). `completeGraphTreeParentCode_exists_active_leaf` (specialising the rank criterion to the tree distance: every nonempty active set has a leaf for the complete-graph spanning-tree parent code). Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |
| §18.5 | **The moment-weighted constrained active sum** (Issue #3954) | **Done (definition + basic API)** | `ClusterExpansion/RootedParentActiveSum.lean`. The central object of the rooted-tree KP leaf-peel induction: `rootedParentActiveSum G par A hclosed k t` is the sum over labellings `ω : {v // v ∈ rootedParentActiveVertices A} → allPolymers G` (the active-vertex subtype) of the moment-weighted activity `∏_v |ω v|^{k v}·(e|t|)^{|ω v|}`, restricted to the labellings satisfying `ω (succ j) ∼ ω (par j)` for every active `j ∈ A` (the coercions `rootedParentActiveChild hj`, `rootedParentActiveParent hclosed hj` lift `succ j` / `par j` into the subtype via `succ_mem_rootedParentActiveVertices` / `hclosed`). `rootedParentActiveVertices_empty` (`= {0}`), `rootedParentActiveChild_coe`, `rootedParentActiveParent_coe`. The subtype `piFinset` with the dependent-membership constraint and the moment weight elaborates with automatic decidability. The base case (`A = ∅`, see next row), the active-subtype coordinate split, the leaf-peel inequality, and the strong induction follow. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |
| §18.5 | **Base case of the active sum (empty active set)** (Issue #3954) | **Done (`rootedParentActiveSum G par ∅ hclosed k t = ∑_P |P|^{k 0}(e|t|)^|P|`)** | `ClusterExpansion/RootedParentActiveSum.lean`. Reference: Glimm–Jaffe, 2nd ed., §18.4–§18.5, pp. 332–336; Friedli–Velenik §5.4 (Theorem 5.4). |

Because the complete-graph spanning-tree parent code injects spanning trees into parent functions `Fin n → Fin (n+1)` (`completeGraphTreeParentCode_injective`), and the child count `rootedParentChildCount (completeGraphTreeParentCode n T) univ` is exactly the parent-function fiber size, `sum_completeGraphTrees_prod_childCount_factorial_le`: `∑_{T} ∏_v (childCount T v)! ≤ ∑_{p : Fin n → Fin (n+1)} ∏_v (fiber count of p at v)!` (`Finset.sum_image` on the injection + `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset`, monotone in ℕ).
